It WRAPS the real observer (live <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> or\n10\t/// <see cref=\"ConsoleRunObserver\"/>), forwards every event verbatim, and AFTER forwarding rewrites\n11\t/// the site through <see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer\"/>:\n12\t/// <list type=\"bullet\">\n13\t///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskStarting\"/> a task flips pending → running and the index is rewritten —\n14\t///     a running task links to the LIVE server (a click tails it) when a server is up, else plain text.</item>\n15\t///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskFinished\"/> a task flips to its settled status, its static page is written\n16\t///     (<see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts\"/>), and the index is rewritten — a\n17\t///     settled task with attempts on disk now links to its static page.</item>\n18\t/// </list>\n19\t///\n20\t/// <para>The index always carries the <c>meta refresh</c> (<c>includeRefresh:true</c>) so a\n21\t/// <c>file://</c> view re-reads it as it is rewritten; the DURABLE final/<c>--export</c> index (no\n22\t/// refresh, all-static) is written separately by the run's end-of-run path, NOT here.</para>\n23\t///\n24\t/// <para>The renderer writes atomically, so a browser never reads a torn file. This decorator's own\n25\t/// status map is the only shared mutable state, and M4 worker threads call in concurrently, so all\n26\t/// access to it — and the write that projects from it — is serialised under one lock. Renders are\n27\t/// best-effort: a render failure (e.g. a transient file lock) is swallowed so a UX nicety never\n28\t/// flips a task's outcome or aborts the run.</para>\n29\t/// </summary>\n30\tpublic sealed class OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver : IRunObserver\n31\t{\n32\t    private readonly IRunObserver _inner;\n33\t    private readonly string _logsRoot;\n34\t    private readonly string _runId;\n35\t    private readonly IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> _tasks;\n36\t    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TaskNode> _tasksById;\n37\t    private readonly Func<string, string?>? _liveUrlForTask;\n38\t\n39\t    // Per-task status word, seeded \"pending\". Mutated and projected under one lock — events arrive\n40\t    // from concurrent M4 workers, and the index render reads the whole map, so the two must not race.\n41\t    private readonly object _gate = new();\n42\t    private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _statusByTask;\n43\t\n44\t    /// <param name=\"inner\">The real observer every event is forwarded to (live or console).</param>\n45\t    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the site is written into.</param>\n46\t    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n47\t    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n48\t    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">\n49\t    /// Resolver mapping a task id to its live-server URL, or null when no server is up. A RUNNING task\n50\t    /// links to this URL (a click tails it) when non-null; null = the running task is plain text.\n51\t    /// </param>\n52\t    public OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver(\n53\t        IRunObserver inner,\n54\t        string logsRoot,\n55\t        string runId,\n56\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n57\t        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n58\t    {\n59\t        _inner = inner ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(inner));\n60\t        _logsRoot = logsRoot;\n61\t        _runId = runId;\n62\t        _tasks = tasks;\n63\t        _tasksById = tasks.ToDictionary(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n64\t        _liveUrlForTask = liveUrlForTask;\n65\t        _statusByTask = tasks.ToDictionary(\n66\t            t => t.Id, _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending), StringComparer.Ordinal);\n67\t    }\n68\t\n69\t    /// <summary>\n70\t    /// Write the initial all-pending index at run start (every task pending, plain text), so the \"all\n71\t    /// tasks\" page exists and is browsable the moment the run begins. Best-effort. Delegates to the\n72\t    /// static <see cref=\"WriteInitialIndex(string, string, IReadOnlyList{TaskNode}, Func{string, string?})\"/>.\n73\t    /// </summary>\n74\t    public void WriteInitialIndex() => WriteInitialIndex(_logsRoot, _runId, _tasks, _liveUrlForTask);\n75\t\n76\t    /// <summary>\n77\t    /// Write the initial all-pending index (every task <c>pending</c>, plain link, with the during-run\n78\t    /// meta-refresh) WITHOUT an observer instance, so the live path can write it — and print the\n79\t    /// link to it — BEFORE constructing <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> (which starts the Spectre\n80\t    /// <c>AnsiConsole.Live</c> region in its ctor). Any console write into an active Live region\n81\t    /// corrupts the table, so the initial index + its static-index link must be emitted first (#145\n82\t    /// Bug 1). Best-effort: a render failure is swallowed (a UX nicety never aborts the run).\n83\t    /// </summary>\n84\t    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the index is written into.</param>\n85\t    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n86\t    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n87\t    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">Unused at the all-pending start (no task is running yet); accepted\n88\t    /// so the static signature matches the instance's link-resolution surface for callers.</param>\n89\t    public static void WriteInitialIndex(\n90\t        string logsRoot,\n91\t        string runId,\n92\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n93\t        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n94\t    {\n95\t        _ = liveUrlForTask; // no task is running at the all-pending start, so no live link is resolved yet\n96\t        string pending = LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending);\n97\t        TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n98\t            logsRoot,\n99\t            runId,\n100\t            tasks,\n101\t            statusResolver: _ => pending,\n102\t            linkResolver: _ => LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain,\n103\t            includeRefresh: true));\n104\t    }\n105\t\n106\t    public void TaskStarting(TaskNode task)\n107\t    {\n108\t        _inner.TaskStarting(task);\n109\t        SetStatus(task.Id, LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running));\n110\t        RenderIndex();\n111\t    }\n112\t\n113\t    public void AttemptStarting(TaskNode task, int attempt, int budget) =>\n114\t        _inner.AttemptStarting(task, attempt, budget);\n115\t\n116\t    public void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result) =>\n117\t        _inner.GuardrailFinished(task, result);\n118\t\n119\t    public void TaskFinished(TaskResult result)\n120\t    {\n121\t        _inner.TaskFinished(result);\n122\t        SetStatus(result.TaskId, StatusWord(result.Outcome));\n123\t\n124\t        // Write the finished task's static page so the index's link to it (and the terminal's\n125\t        // post-mortem link, #141 item 1) resolves to a rendered page, not a 404.\n126\t        if (_tasksById.TryGetValue(result.TaskId, out TaskNode? task))\n127\t        {\n128\t            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts(_logsRoot, task));\n129\t        }\n130\t\n131\t        RenderIndex();\n132\t    }\n133\t\n134\t    public void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) => _inner.PlanHashMismatch(previousPlanHash);\n135\t\n136\t    public void ParallelismClampedNoProvider(int requested) => _inner.ParallelismClampedNoProvider(requested);\n137\t\n138\t    public void CleanupFailed(string owner, Exception error) => _inner.CleanupFailed(owner, error);\n139\t\n140\t    public void PromptPaused(TaskNode task, string reason, TimeSpan backoff, int pauseCount) =>\n141\t        _inner.PromptPaused(task, reason, backoff, pauseCount);\n142\t\n143\t    // --- site projection --------------------------------------------------------------------\n144\t\n145\t    private void SetStatus(string taskId, string status)\n146\t    {\n147\t        lock (_gate)\n148\t        {\n149\t            _statusByTask[taskId] = status;\n150\t        }\n151\t    }\n152\t\n153\t    /// <summary>\n154\t    /// Rewrite the during-run index (with refresh) from the current status map. Holds the lock for the\n155\t    /// whole render so the status snapshot and the link choice are consistent (the renderer writes\n156\t    /// atomically). The link resolver: a RUNNING task → the live URL when a server is up (else plain),\n157\t    /// any task with attempts on disk → its static page, anything else → plain text.\n158\t    /// </summary>\n159\t    private void RenderIndex()\n160\t    {\n161\t        lock (_gate)\n162\t        {\n163\t            // Snapshot the statuses inside the lock so the resolver closures read a stable view.\n164\t            var statuses = new Dictionary<string, string>(_statusByTask, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n165\t            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n166\t                _logsRoot,\n167\t                _runId,\n168\t                _tasks,\n169\t                statusResolver: id => statuses.TryGetValue(id, out string? s) ? s : \"unknown\",\n170\t                linkResolver: id => ResolveLink(id, statuses),\n171\t                includeRefresh: true));\n172\t        }\n173\t    }\n174\t\n175\t    private LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink ResolveLink(string taskId, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> statuses)\n176\t    {\n177\t        bool running = statuses.TryGetValue(taskId, out string? status) &&\n178\t                       status == LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running);\n179\t\n180\t        // A running task links to the live server (a click tails it) when one is up; otherwise it is\n181\t        // plain text (no static page to point at yet).\n182\t        if (running && _liveUrlForTask?.Invoke(taskId) is { } liveUrl)\n183\t        {\n184\t            return LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.LiveTo(liveUrl);\n185\t        }\n186\t\n187\t        // A task with attempts on disk (running-without-server, or settled) links to its static page;\n188\t        // a pending/no-attempt task is plain text.\n189\t        return HasAttempts(taskId) ? LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Static : LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain;\n190\t    }\n191\t\n192\t    private bool HasAttempts(string taskId)\n193\t    {\n194\t        string taskDir = Path.Combine(_logsRoot, taskId);\n195\t        if (!Directory.Exists(taskDir))\n196\t        {\n197\t            return false;\n198\t        }\n199\t\n200\t        return Directory.EnumerateDirectories(taskDir)\n201\t            .Any(d => Path.GetFileName(d).StartsWith(\"attempt-\", StringComparison.Ordinal));\n202\t    }\n203\t\n204\t    /// <summary>Map a finished task's outcome to the index status word (mirrors the journal mapping).</summary>\n205\t    private static string StatusWord(TaskOutcome outcome) => outcome switch\n206\t    {\n207\t        TaskOutcome.Succeeded => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Succeeded),\n208\t        TaskOutcome.Skipped => \"skipped\",\n209\t        TaskOutcome.Blocked => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Blocked),\n210\t        TaskOutcome.Cancelled => \"cancelled\",\n211\t        // ActionFailed / GuardrailFailed / InvalidFragment / NeedsHuman are all needs-human terminal.\n212\t        _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.NeedsHuman),\n213\t    };\n214\t\n215\t    /// <summary>\n216\t    /// Run a render action, swallowing IO failures: the on-the-fly site is a UX nicety and must never\n217\t    /// flip a task's outcome or abort the run. A transient lock/torn-read is retried by the next event.\n218\t    /// </summary>\n219\t    private static void TryRender(Action render)\n220\t    {\n221\t        try\n222\t        {\n223\t            render();\n224\t        }\n225\t        catch (IOException)\n226\t        {\n227\t            // best-effort — the next event re-renders\n228\t        }\n229\t        catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)\n230\t        {\n231\t            // best-effort — never let a logs-tree permission hiccup abort the run\n232\t        }\n233\t    }\n234\t}\n235\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"da2e2042-c4b6-4ef5-b6ac-18dee996d70e","uuid":"90ddbb23-99eb-4731-8ff2-ea1279a5e2eb","timestamp":"2026-07-07T17:10:52.737Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Dev AI\\Guardrails\\src\\Guardrails.Cli\\Ui\\OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver.cs","content":"using Guardrails.Core.Execution;\nusing Guardrails.Core.Model;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Cli.Ui;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// A decorator <see cref=\"IRunObserver\"/> that keeps the DURING-RUN static log site\n/// (<c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/index.html</c> + per-task pages) up to date as the run proceeds (issue #141\n/// item 2). Renders are\n/// best-effort: a render failure (e.g. a transient file lock) is swallowed so a UX nicety never\n/// flips a task's outcome or aborts the run.</para>\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver : IRunObserver\n{\n    private readonly IRunObserver _inner;\n    private readonly string _logsRoot;\n    private readonly string _runId;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> _tasks;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TaskNode> _tasksById;\n    private readonly Func<string, string?>? _liveUrlForTask;\n\n    // Per-task status word, seeded \"pending\". Mutated and projected under one lock — events arrive\n    // from concurrent M4 workers, and the index render reads the whole map, so the two must not race.\n    private readonly object _gate = new();\n    private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _statusByTask;\n\n    /// <param name=\"inner\">The real observer every event is forwarded to (live or console).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the site is written into.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">\n    /// Resolver mapping a task id to its live-server URL, or null when no server is up. A RUNNING task\n    /// links to this URL (a click tails it) when non-null; null = the running task is plain text.\n    /// </param>\n    public OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver(\n        IRunObserver inner,\n        string logsRoot,\n        string runId,\n        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n    {\n        _inner = inner ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(inner));\n        _logsRoot = logsRoot;\n        _runId = runId;\n        _tasks = tasks;\n        _tasksById = tasks.ToDictionary(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n        _liveUrlForTask = liveUrlForTask;\n        _statusByTask = tasks.ToDictionary(\n            t => t.Id, _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending), StringComparer.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Write the initial all-pending index at run start (every task pending, plain text), so the \"all\n    /// tasks\" page exists and is browsable the moment the run begins. Best-effort. Delegates to the\n    /// static <see cref=\"WriteInitialIndex(string, string, IReadOnlyList{TaskNode}, Func{string, string?})\"/>.\n    /// </summary>\n    public void WriteInitialIndex() => WriteInitialIndex(_logsRoot, _runId, _tasks, _liveUrlForTask);\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Write the initial all-pending index (every task <c>pending</c>, plain link, with the during-run\n    /// meta-refresh) WITHOUT an observer instance, so the live path can write it — and print the\n    /// link to it — BEFORE constructing <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> (which starts the Spectre\n    /// <c>AnsiConsole.Live</c> region in its ctor). Any console write into an active Live region\n    /// corrupts the table, so the initial index + its static-index link must be emitted first (#145\n    /// Bug 1). Best-effort: a render failure is swallowed (a UX nicety never aborts the run).\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the index is written into.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">Unused at the all-pending start (no task is running yet); accepted\n    /// so the static signature matches the instance's link-resolution surface for callers.</param>\n    public static void WriteInitialIndex(\n        string logsRoot,\n        string runId,\n        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n    {\n        _ = liveUrlForTask; // no task is running at the all-pending start, so no live link is resolved yet\n        string pending = LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending);\n        TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n            logsRoot,\n            runId,\n            tasks,\n            statusResolver: _ => pending,\n            linkResolver: _ => LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain,\n            includeRefresh: true));\n    }\n\n    public void TaskStarting(TaskNode task)\n    {\n        _inner.TaskStarting(task);\n        SetStatus(task.Id, LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running));\n        RenderIndex();\n    }\n\n    public void AttemptStarting(TaskNode task, int attempt, int budget) =>\n        _inner.AttemptStarting(task, attempt, budget);\n\n    public void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result) =>\n        _inner.GuardrailFinished(task, result);\n\n    public void TaskFinished(TaskResult result)\n    {\n        _inner.TaskFinished(result);\n        SetStatus(result.TaskId, StatusWord(result.Outcome));\n\n        // Write the finished task's static page so the index's link to it (and the terminal's\n        // post-mortem link, #141 item 1) resolves to a rendered page, not a 404.\n        if (_tasksById.TryGetValue(result.TaskId, out TaskNode? task))\n        {\n            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts(_logsRoot, task));\n        }\n\n        RenderIndex();\n    }\n\n    public void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) => _inner.PlanHashMismatch(previousPlanHash);\n\n    public void ParallelismClampedNoProvider(int requested) => _inner.ParallelismClampedNoProvider(requested);\n\n    public void CleanupFailed(string owner, Exception error) => _inner.CleanupFailed(owner, error);\n\n    public void PromptPaused(TaskNode task, string reason, TimeSpan backoff, int pauseCount) =>\n        _inner.PromptPaused(task, reason, backoff, pauseCount);\n\n    // --- site projection --------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    private void SetStatus(string taskId, string status)\n    {\n        lock (_gate)\n        {\n            _statusByTask[taskId] = status;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Rewrite the during-run index (with refresh) from the current status map. Holds the lock for the\n    /// whole render so the status snapshot and the link choice are consistent (the renderer writes\n    /// atomically). The link resolver: a RUNNING task → the live URL when a server is up (else plain),\n    /// any task with attempts on disk → its static page, anything else → plain text.\n    /// </summary>\n    private void RenderIndex()\n    {\n        lock (_gate)\n        {\n            // Snapshot the statuses inside the lock so the resolver closures read a stable view.\n            var statuses = new Dictionary<string, string>(_statusByTask, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n                _logsRoot,\n                _runId,\n                _tasks,\n                statusResolver: id => statuses.TryGetValue(id, out string? s) ? s : \"unknown\",\n                linkResolver: id => ResolveLink(id, statuses),\n                includeRefresh: true));\n        }\n    }\n\n    private LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink ResolveLink(string taskId, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> statuses)\n    {\n        bool running = statuses.TryGetValue(taskId, out string? status) &&\n                       status == LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running);\n\n        // A running task links to the live server (a click tails it) when one is up; otherwise it is\n        // plain text (no static page to point at yet).\n        if (running && _liveUrlForTask?.Invoke(taskId) is { } liveUrl)\n        {\n            return LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.LiveTo(liveUrl);\n        }\n\n        // A task with attempts on disk (running-without-server, or settled) links to its static page;\n        // a pending/no-attempt task is plain text.\n        return HasAttempts(taskId) ? LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Static : LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain;\n    }\n\n    private bool HasAttempts(string taskId)\n    {\n        string taskDir = Path.Combine(_logsRoot, taskId);\n        if (!Directory.Exists(taskDir))\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        return Directory.EnumerateDirectories(taskDir)\n            .Any(d => Path.GetFileName(d).StartsWith(\"attempt-\", StringComparison.Ordinal));\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Map a finished task's outcome to the index status word (mirrors the journal mapping).</summary>\n    private static string StatusWord(TaskOutcome outcome) => outcome switch\n    {\n        TaskOutcome.Succeeded => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Succeeded),\n        TaskOutcome.Skipped => \"skipped\",\n        TaskOutcome.Blocked => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Blocked),\n        TaskOutcome.Cancelled => \"cancelled\",\n        // ActionFailed / GuardrailFailed / InvalidFragment / NeedsHuman are all needs-human terminal.\n        _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.NeedsHuman),\n    };\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Run a render action, swallowing IO failures: the on-the-fly site is a UX nicety and must never\n    /// flip a task's outcome or abort the run. A transient lock/torn-read is retried by the next event.\n    /// </summary>\n    private static void TryRender(Action render)\n    {\n        try\n        {\n            render();\n        }\n        catch (IOException)\n        {\n            // best-effort — the next event re-renders\n        }\n        catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)\n        {\n            // best-effort — never let a logs-tree permission hiccup abort the run\n        }\n    }\n}\n","numLines":235,"startLine":1,"totalLines":235}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SLNe1sJZFtd2cGK5MXuhf4","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tusing System.Text.Encodings.Web;\n2\tusing System.Text.Json;\n3\t\n4\tnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n5\t\n6\t/// <summary>\n7\t/// Renders the local-viewing companion to <c>diagram.md</c>: a self-contained\n8\t/// <c>diagram.html</c> that displays the SAME Mermaid DAG with pan / zoom / fullscreen, so a\n9\t/// large task+guardrail graph is actually navigable on disk (GitHub renders <c>diagram.md</c>\n10\t/// but offers no navigation). Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its <c>source-sha256</c>\n11\t/// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33).\n12\t/// </summary>\n13\t/// <remarks>\n14\t/// <para>\n15\t/// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a\n16\t/// <c>&lt;script type=\"text/plain\"&gt;</c> element and read back via <c>textContent</c> — never\n17\t/// interpolated into a JS string. This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a\n18\t/// backtick, <c>${</c>, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <c>&lt;script&gt;</c> element's\n19\t/// content is \"raw text\" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte.\n20\t/// This is safe because <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> HTML-escapes every label (so <c>&lt;</c>\n21\t/// becomes <c>&amp;lt;</c>), meaning the source can never contain <c>&lt;/script&gt;</c>.\n22\t/// </para>\n23\t/// <para>\n24\t/// The <c>source-sha256</c> provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before\n25\t/// <c>&lt;!doctype html&gt;</c>) so the same <c>\\A</c>-anchored reader that validates\n26\t/// <c>diagram.md</c> validates this file too (<c>graph --check</c>). A comment before the\n27\t/// doctype does not trigger quirks mode.\n28\t/// </para>\n29\t/// <para>\n30\t/// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs\n31\t/// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the\n32\t/// LOCAL artifact; <c>diagram.md</c> remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets)\n33\t/// is a possible follow-up.\n34\t/// </para>\n35\t/// <para>\n36\t/// <b>Legend overlay.</b> A corner-anchored <c>#legend</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>\n37\t/// (<c>position: fixed</c>), mirroring the existing <c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> overlay divs, renders\n38\t/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.LegendMarkdown\"/>'s content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native\n39\t/// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN —\n40\t/// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\" overlapping the real DAG — so\n41\t/// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from\n42\t/// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on <c>source-sha256</c>.\n43\t/// </para>\n44\t/// <para>\n45\t/// <b>Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233\n46\t/// superseded, issue #235).</b> A Mermaid <c>click</c> directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster\n47\t/// element (upstream limitation; see <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> remarks), and the first fix\n48\t/// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre\n49\t/// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container\n50\t/// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail\n51\t/// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves: for every\n52\t/// <c>g.cluster</c> element whose id starts with <c>task_</c>, compute a full-width band from the\n53\t/// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its <c>.cluster-label</c>'s bottom edge (Mermaid\n54\t/// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION\n55\t/// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and\n56\t/// append a real <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c>\n57\t/// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its\n58\t/// background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c> then its <c>.cluster-label</c> group, so appending puts the\n59\t/// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text\n60\t/// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely\n61\t/// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's <c>g.cluster</c> — the overlay can never\n62\t/// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data\n63\t/// this script needs (<see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) is embedded as a small JSON\n64\t/// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a\n65\t/// <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"&gt;</c> element read back via <c>textContent</c> (same\n66\t/// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping\n67\t/// hazards).\n68\t/// </para>\n69\t/// <para>\n70\t/// <b>Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject\n71\t/// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow).</b> Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title\n72\t/// <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>'s plain\n73\t/// flowchart cluster shape never overrides <c>createText</c>'s <c>width = 200</c> default,\n74\t/// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout\n75\t/// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a\n76\t/// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines\n77\t/// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned\n78\t/// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — <c>flowchart.htmlLabels</c> only toggles\n79\t/// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label\n80\t/// wrap width. The fix (the <c>fixWrappedClusterLabels</c> function, run AFTER\n81\t/// <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's\n82\t/// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the\n83\t/// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already\n84\t/// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than\n85\t/// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. Verified\n86\t/// headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names): every wrapped case converged to one line\n87\t/// with the same healthy gap a never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label\n88\t/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n89\t/// </para>\n90\t/// </remarks>\n91\tpublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer\n92\t{\n93\t    /// <summary>\n94\t    /// Build the <c>diagram.html</c> document for <paramref name=\"mermaidSource\"/> (the exact\n95\t    /// text rendered into <c>diagram.md</c>, including the <c>flowchart TD</c> header and the\n96\t    /// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> lines) stamped with <paramref name=\"sourceHash\"/>. <paramref\n97\t    /// name=\"taskFolderTargets\"/> is the task-container-id → plan-relative-folder-path map (see\n98\t    /// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) the embedded title-band overlay script uses\n99\t    /// to resolve each container's click target (issue #235 — see class remarks).\n100\t    /// </summary>\n101\t    public static string Render(\n102\t        string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets)\n103\t    {\n104\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(mermaidSource);\n105\t        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty(sourceHash);\n106\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(taskFolderTargets);\n107\t\n108\t        // Newline-normalize so the file is byte-identical across OSes (mirrors the renderer/hash).\n109\t        string source = mermaidSource\n110\t            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n111\t            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n112\t            .TrimEnd('\\n');\n113\t\n114\t        // Encoder that escapes NOTHING beyond what JSON strictly requires (default System.Text.Json\n115\t        // escapes '<', '>', '&', etc. as \\uXXXX for HTML safety, which is unnecessary here — the\n116\t        // JSON sits inside a <script type=\"application/json\"> element, read back via textContent,\n117\t        // exactly like the Mermaid source above — but using the unsafe-relaxed encoder keeps a\n118\t        // task-id containing e.g. \"&\" readable in the raw HTML source without changing behavior).\n119\t        string targetsJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(taskFolderTargets, new JsonSerializerOptions\n120\t        {\n121\t            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n122\t        });\n123\t\n124\t        // Normalize the full output — the template raw-string literal picks up \\r\\n when the\n125\t        // file is checked out with CRLF on Windows; the mermaid source is already normalized above.\n126\t        return Template\n127\t            .Replace(\"__SOURCE_SHA256__\", sourceHash, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n128\t            .Replace(\"__GRAPH_SOURCE__\", source, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n129\t            .Replace(\"__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__\", targetsJson, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n130\t            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n131\t            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n132\t    }\n133\t\n134\t    // __SOURCE_SHA256__ is filled with a lowercase-hex hash (no escaping needed). __GRAPH_SOURCE__\n135\t    // is filled with the verbatim Mermaid text inside a raw-text <script> element (see remarks).\n136\t    // __TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__ is filled with a JSON object (container id -> folder path).\n137\t    private const string Template = \"\"\"\n138\t<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256=__SOURCE_SHA256__ -->\n139\t<!doctype html>\n140\t<html lang=\"en\">\n141\t<head>\n142\t<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n143\t<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n144\t<title>Guardrails — task/guardrail DAG</title>\n145\t<style>\n146\t  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; background: #0b0f14; color: #d6deeb;\n147\t               font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; }\n148\t  #bar { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; z-index: 10; display: flex; gap: 6px; }\n149\t  #bar button { background: #121a24; color: #d6deeb; border: 1px solid #243343;\n150\t                border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 10px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; }\n151\t  #bar button:hover { border-color: #7fdbff; }\n152\t  #stage { width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }\n153\t  #stage svg { width: 100vw; height: 100vh; max-width: none !important; }\n154\t  #hint { position: fixed; bottom: 8px; left: 8px; color: #5b6b7b; font-size: 12px;\n155\t          max-width: 90vw; }\n156\t  #legend { position: fixed; top: 8px; right: 8px; z-index: 10; background: #121a24;\n157\t            border: 1px solid #243343; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px;\n158\t            font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; }\n159\t  #legend .swatch { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px;\n160\t                    margin-right: 6px; }\n161\t</style>\n162\t</head>\n163\t<body>\n164\t<div id=\"bar\">\n165\t  <button id=\"fit\">Fit</button>\n166\t  <button id=\"zin\">+</button>\n167\t  <button id=\"zout\">&minus;</button>\n168\t  <button id=\"fs\">Fullscreen</button>\n169\t</div>\n170\t<div id=\"stage\"></div>\n171\t<div id=\"legend\">\n172\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#e6d7ff;border:1px solid #6f42c1;\"></span>\n173\t    <b>Preflight</b> &mdash; verified BEFORE the task's attempt loop; gates entry\n174\t    (dependency-delivery precondition)</div>\n175\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#fff3cd;border:1px solid #b8860b;\"></span>\n176\t    <b>Guardrail</b> &mdash; verified AFTER the task's action; must pass for the task to finish</div>\n177\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#d4edda;border:1px solid #2e7d32;\"></span>\n178\t    Plan-level containers (\"Full Flight Checks\" top, \"Terminal Gate\" bottom) run the same two\n179\t    checks once for the whole plan, at the very start and very end.</div>\n180\t</div>\n181\t<div id=\"hint\">scroll = zoom &middot; drag = pan &middot; Fit resets &middot; Fullscreen (or press F11).\n182\t  Node clicks open source files &mdash; serve via a local HTTP server (e.g.\n183\t  <code>python -m http.server</code>) for clicks to work; browsers block\n184\t  <code>file://&rarr;file://</code> navigation by default.\n185\t  On GitHub, diagram.md renders instead.</div>\n186\t\n187\t<script type=\"text/plain\" id=\"graph-source\">__GRAPH_SOURCE__</script>\n188\t<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"task-folder-targets\">__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__</script>\n189\t<script src=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js\"></script>\n190\t<script type=\"module\">\n191\timport mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';\n192\t\n193\tconst graph = document.getElementById('graph-source').textContent;\n194\tconst taskFolderTargets = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('task-folder-targets').textContent);\n195\t// securityLevel 'loose' is required for the `click ... href` directives to open node sources;\n196\t// the content is the user's own local plan, served from file:// — not untrusted input.\n197\t// maxTextSize raises Mermaid's default 50 000-character source ceiling (issue #108): a large\n198\t// plan's DAG source easily exceeds it, and on overflow mermaid.render throws \"Maximum text size\n199\t// in diagram exceeded\" — landing every big plan in the catch-block \"could not render\" fallback.\n200\t// 5 000 000 covers DAGs far larger than any hand-reviewed plan while still bounding the parser.\n201\t// maxEdges raises Mermaid's default 500-edge ceiling for the same reason: a many-task plan fans\n202\t// out task→guardrail→done→dependent edges well past 500, and overflow throws \"Maximum number of\n203\t// edges exceeded\". Both ceilings must be lifted or a big plan still fails to render.\n204\tmermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'loose', maxTextSize: 5000000, maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: { useMaxWidth: false } });\n205\t\n206\t// Widen a wrapped cluster-title's foreignObject so a long kebab-case task name reflows onto\n207\t// FEWER lines instead of overflowing Mermaid's fixed header-strip reservation (issue\n208\t// cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Root cause, confirmed against the bundled mermaid@11.4.1 source\n209\t// (`src/rendering-util/createText.ts`'s `createText(el, text, { width = 200 })` default, which\n210\t// the plain flowchart \"rect\" cluster shape never overrides): a cluster's title <div> is always\n211\t// wrapped to a hardcoded 200px width regardless of the container's own — usually much wider —\n212\t// computed width, and dagre's LAYOUT PASS reserves header space for the container BEFORE that\n213\t// wrapped height is known, so it never grows to fit more than a couple of lines. A short label\n214\t// fits on one line inside 200px with room to spare (a healthy ~13px gap above the first leaf\n215\t// node, measured); a long name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) wraps to 2 or more\n216\t// lines, and each line beyond the first prints a full line-height PAST what dagre reserved —\n217\t// landing on top of the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned directly below.\n218\t//\n219\t// Two Mermaid config knobs were checked and ruled out first: `flowchart.htmlLabels` only toggles\n220\t// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer (not label width), and 11.4.1 has no documented\n221\t// `flowchart`/theme-variable option for cluster-label wrapping width — 200 is a hardcoded\n222\t// parameter default the cluster-shape renderer never overrides, not a configurable value.\n223\t//\n224\t// The fix instead re-wraps the SAME text into fewer lines post-render: a task container is\n225\t// normally already wider than 200px (dagre sized it to fit its leaf content), so letting the\n226\t// identical label reflow at (up to) the container's own width almost always drops it to one\n227\t// line, which needs LESS height than Mermaid's original wrap — never more. That means this can\n228\t// only ever shrink the label's footprint, never grow it, so no other node/edge/container ever\n229\t// needs to move to make room. Verified headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names,\n230\t// container widths from ~230px to ~1100px, wraps from 2 to 3 lines): every case converged to one\n231\t// line with the same healthy negative gap a short, never-wrapped label already has; every\n232\t// already-fits-on-one-line label (including every task in the golden `hello-guardrails` example)\n233\t// was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n234\tfunction fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl) {\n235\t  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n236\t  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n237\t    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n238\t    if (!label) continue;\n239\t    const fo = label.querySelector('foreignObject');\n240\t    const div = fo ? fo.querySelector('div') : null;\n241\t    if (!fo || !div) continue;\n242\t\n243\t    const currentWidth = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('width')) || 0;\n244\t    const currentHeight = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('height')) || 0;\n245\t    if (currentWidth <= 0 || currentHeight <= 0) continue;\n246\t\n247\t    // scrollWidth/scrollHeight are LOCAL layout-box measurements in the foreignObject's own\n248\t    // SVG-user-unit coordinate system — deliberately NOT the screen-space rect API (see class\n249\t    // remarks): a screen-space read is affected by every ancestor SVG transform (dagre's per-node\n250\t    // translate, the pan-zoom viewport's zoom/pan matrix), so it would be misleading compared\n251\t    // against the foreignObject's own width/height attributes. Measure the label's natural\n252\t    // single-line width by temporarily lifting the wrap constraint Mermaid applied, then restore\n253\t    // it immediately.\n254\t    const savedInline = div.getAttribute('style');\n255\t    div.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n256\t    div.style.width = 'auto';\n257\t    div.style.maxWidth = 'none';\n258\t    // +2px safety buffer: scrollWidth can round down a hair short of the true subpixel width\n259\t    // needed for one line (observed empirically — re-applying the exact measured value as a\n260\t    // fixed width sometimes still wrapped to 2 lines by a fraction of a pixel).\n261\t    const naturalWidth = div.scrollWidth + 2;\n262\t    div.setAttribute('style', savedInline); // restore Mermaid's original wrapped styling\n263\t\n264\t    if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue; // already fits on one line — untouched\n265\t\n266\t    // Never widen past the cluster's own body (leave a small margin) — the container's leaf\n267\t    // content already determined this width, so the label can use up to it without ever moving\n268\t    // a leaf node, edge, or sibling container. Never NARROWER than Mermaid's original width either\n269\t    // — this only ever grows the box.\n270\t    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n271\t    const newWidth = Math.min(naturalWidth, Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16));\n272\t\n273\t    div.style.whiteSpace = 'break-spaces';\n274\t    div.style.display = 'table';\n275\t    div.style.width = newWidth + 'px';\n276\t    div.style.maxWidth = newWidth + 'px';\n277\t    const newHeight = div.scrollHeight;\n278\t\n279\t    if (newHeight >= currentHeight) {\n280\t      // Widening did not actually reduce the wrapped height (the cluster is too narrow to fit\n281\t      // even one more character per line) — revert rather than risk an oddly-proportioned label.\n282\t      div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\n283\t      continue;\n284\t    }\n285\t\n286\t    fo.setAttribute('width', String(newWidth));\n287\t    fo.setAttribute('height', String(newHeight));\n288\t\n289\t    // Mermaid centers the label group on the cluster's horizontal midpoint via\n290\t    // `translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y)`; widening the box without re-centering would shift it\n291\t    // left of center, so shift the existing translate by half the width delta to keep it on the\n292\t    // SAME midpoint. The label's y stays fixed — only its height shrank, so its bottom edge\n293\t    // simply moves UP, further from the first leaf node, never displacing it.\n294\t    const transform = label.getAttribute('transform') || '';\n295\t    const match = transform.match(/translate\\(([-\\d.eE]+)\\s*,\\s*([-\\d.eE]+)\\)/);\n296\t    if (match) {\n297\t      const oldX = parseFloat(match[1]);\n298\t      const deltaCenter = (newWidth - currentWidth) / 2;\n299\t      label.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${oldX - deltaCenter}, ${match[2]})`);\n300\t    }\n301\t  }\n302\t}\n303\t\n304\t// Inject a real clickable overlay on each task container's TITLE/LABEL ROW (issue #232/#233\n305\t// superseded, issue #235). Mermaid never fires a `click` directive on a subgraph/cluster element,\n306\t// and an anchor NODE inside the container gets packed into whatever sliver of space dagre's own\n307\t// layout leaves — useless for a content-dense container. The title band is different: Mermaid\n308\t// ALWAYS renders a cluster as exactly two children, a background <rect> then a <g\n309\t// class=\"cluster-label\">, with the label in its own reserved header strip above any leaf content —\n310\t// so a full-width band from the cluster's top down to just past the label's bottom edge is empty BY\n311\t// CONSTRUCTION, regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has. Must run AFTER\n312\t// fixWrappedClusterLabels (above): the band height is measured from the label's CURRENT bbox, so\n313\t// a label that fixWrappedClusterLabels already shrank back to one line gets a correspondingly\n314\t// short band, not one sized for its original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n315\tfunction addTaskContainerOverlays(svgEl) {\n316\t  const ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';\n317\t  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n318\t  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n319\t    const target = taskFolderTargets[cluster.id];\n320\t    if (!target) continue; // not a task container (e.g. plan_preflights/plan_guardrails), or no map entry\n321\t    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n322\t    if (!label) continue;\n323\t\n324\t    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n325\t    const labelBox = label.getBBox();\n326\t    const bandHeight = (labelBox.y + labelBox.height) - clusterBox.y + 8; // small padding below the title\n327\t\n328\t    const a = document.createElementNS(ns, 'a');\n329\t    a.setAttribute('href', target);\n330\t    a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');\n331\t    a.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open task folder: ' + target);\n332\t\n333\t    const rect = document.createElementNS(ns, 'rect');\n334\t    rect.setAttribute('x', String(clusterBox.x));\n335\t    rect.setAttribute('y', String(clusterBox.y));\n336\t    rect.setAttribute('width', String(clusterBox.width));\n337\t    rect.setAttribute('height', String(bandHeight));\n338\t    // Inline style (not the `fill` ATTRIBUTE) deliberately: Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n339\t    // carries a rule like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}` that colors every cluster's\n340\t    // background rect. Since this overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group (so it stays in\n341\t    // the same paint context as the background rect it sits atop), that same selector matches it\n342\t    // too — and a CSS class/tag selector beats a plain presentation attribute, so `fill=\"transparent\"`\n343\t    // as an attribute got silently overridden, painting a solid theme-colored bar over the title text.\n344\t    // An inline style wins over any external/embedded stylesheet rule (short of `!important`), so it\n345\t    // reliably stays invisible regardless of Mermaid's theme.\n346\t    rect.style.fill = 'transparent';\n347\t    rect.style.cursor = 'pointer';\n348\t\n349\t    a.appendChild(rect);\n350\t    // Append as the LAST child — do NOT prepend as the first child. A cluster's only two original\n351\t    // children are its background <rect> then its .cluster-label group (in that paint order).\n352\t    // Appending puts the overlay on top of the background rect (so it is actually clickable)\n353\t    // without covering the label text visually (the rect is transparent either way) — prepending\n354\t    // instead would put the overlay BEHIND the background rect (which becomes second-in-order and\n355\t    // paints over it), silently blocking every click.\n356\t    cluster.appendChild(a);\n357\t  }\n358\t}\n359\t\n360\tlet pz = null;\n361\ttry {\n362\t  const { svg } = await mermaid.render('dag', graph);\n363\t  document.getElementById('stage').innerHTML = svg;\n364\t  const el = document.querySelector('#stage svg');\n365\t  el.setAttribute('width', '100vw');\n366\t  el.setAttribute('height', '100vh');\n367\t  fixWrappedClusterLabels(el);\n368\t  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\n369\t  pz = svgPanZoom(el, { zoomEnabled: true, controlIconsEnabled: false, fit: true, center: true,\n370\t                        minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\n371\t  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\n372\t} catch (e) {\n373\t  // Surface the actual failure (offline CDN, or a Mermaid limit we have not yet lifted) instead of\n374\t  // guessing — a generic \"offline?\" message sent every big-plan #108 failure down the wrong path.\n375\t  const detail = (e && e.message) ? Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its <c>source-sha256</c>\n/// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33).\n/// </summary>\n/// <remarks>\n/// <para>\n/// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"text/plain\"&gt;</c> element and read back via <c>textContent</c> — never\n/// interpolated into a JS string. A comment before the\n/// doctype does not trigger quirks mode.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs\n/// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the\n/// LOCAL artifact; <c>diagram.md</c> remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets)\n/// is a possible follow-up.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Legend overlay.</b> A corner-anchored <c>#legend</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>\n/// (<c>position: fixed</c>), mirroring the existing <c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> overlay divs, renders\n/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.LegendMarkdown\"/>'s content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native\n/// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN —\n/// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\" overlapping the real DAG — so\n/// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from\n/// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on <c>source-sha256</c>.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233\n/// superseded, issue #235).</b> A Mermaid <c>click</c> directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster\n/// element (upstream limitation; see <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> remarks), and the first fix\n/// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre\n/// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container\n/// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail\n/// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves: for every\n/// <c>g.cluster</c> element whose id starts with <c>task_</c>, compute a full-width band from the\n/// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its <c>.cluster-label</c>'s bottom edge (Mermaid\n/// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION\n/// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and\n/// append a real <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c>\n/// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its\n/// background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c> then its <c>.cluster-label</c> group, so appending puts the\n/// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text\n/// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely\n/// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's <c>g.cluster</c> — the overlay can never\n/// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data\n/// this script needs (<see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) is embedded as a small JSON\n/// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"&gt;</c> element read back via <c>textContent</c> (same\n/// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping\n/// hazards).\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject\n/// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow).</b> Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title\n/// <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>'s plain\n/// flowchart cluster shape never overrides <c>createText</c>'s <c>width = 200</c> default,\n/// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout\n/// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a\n/// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines\n/// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned\n/// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — <c>flowchart.htmlLabels</c> only toggles\n/// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label\n/// wrap width. The fix (the <c>fixWrappedClusterLabels</c> function, run AFTER\n/// <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's\n/// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the\n/// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already\n/// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than\n/// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. Verified\n/// headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names): every wrapped case converged to one line\n/// with the same healthy gap a never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label\n/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n/// </para>\n/// </remarks>\npublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer\n{\n    /// <summary>\n    public static string Render(\n        string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets)\n    {\n Newline-normalize so the file is byte-identical across OSes (mirrors the renderer/hash).\n        string source = mermaidSource\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n    string targetsJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(taskFolderTargets, new JsonSerializerOptions\n        {\n            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n        });\n\n        // Normalize the full output — the template raw-string literal picks up \\r\\n when the\n        // file is checked out with CRLF on Windows; the mermaid source is already normalized above.\n .Replace(\"__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__\", targetsJson, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // __SOURCE_SHA256__ is filled with a lowercase-hex hash (no escaping needed). __GRAPH_SOURCE__\n    // is filled with the verbatim Mermaid text inside a raw-text <script> element (see remarks).\n    // __TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__ is filled with a JSON object (container id -> folder path).\n    private const string Template = \"\"\"\n<!-- guardrails:graph type=\"module\">\nimport mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';\n\nconst graph = document.getElementById('graph-source').textContent;\nconst taskFolderTargets = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('task-folder-targets').textContent);\n// securityLevel 'loose' is required for the `click ... href` directives to open node sources;\n// the content is the user's own local plan, served from file:// — not untrusted input.\n// maxTextSize raises Mermaid's default 50 000-character source ceiling (issue #108): a large\n// plan's DAG source easily exceeds it, and on overflow mermaid.render throws \"Maximum text size\n// in diagram exceeded\" — landing every big plan in the catch-block \"could not render\" fallback.\n// 5 000 000 covers DAGs far larger than any hand-reviewed plan while still bounding the parser.\n// maxEdges raises Mermaid's default 500-edge ceiling for the same reason: a many-task plan fans\n// out task→guardrail→done→dependent edges well past 500, and overflow throws \"Maximum number of\n// edges exceeded\". Both ceilings must be lifted or a big plan still fails to render.\nmermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'loose', maxTextSize: 5000000, maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: { useMaxWidth: false } });\n\n// Widen a wrapped cluster-title's foreignObject so a long kebab-case task name reflows onto\n// FEWER lines instead of overflowing Mermaid's fixed header-strip reservation (issue\n// cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Root cause, confirmed against the bundled mermaid@11.4.1 source\n// (`src/rendering-util/createText.ts`'s `createText(el, text, { width = 200 })` default, which\n// the plain flowchart \"rect\" cluster shape never overrides): a cluster's title <div> is always\n// wrapped to a hardcoded 200px width regardless of the container's own — usually much wider —\n// computed width, and dagre's LAYOUT PASS reserves header space for the container BEFORE that\n// wrapped height is known, so it never grows to fit more than a couple of lines. A short label\n// fits on one line inside 200px with room to spare (a healthy ~13px gap above the first leaf\n// node, measured); a long name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) wraps to 2 or more\n// lines, and each line beyond the first prints a full line-height PAST what dagre reserved —\n// landing on top of the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned directly below.\n//\n// Two Mermaid config knobs were checked and ruled out first: `flowchart.htmlLabels` only toggles\n// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer (not label width), and 11.4.1 has no documented\n// `flowchart`/theme-variable option for cluster-label wrapping width — 200 is a hardcoded\n// parameter default the cluster-shape renderer never overrides, not a configurable value.\n//\n// The fix instead re-wraps the SAME text into fewer lines post-render: a task container is\n// normally already wider than 200px (dagre sized it to fit its leaf content), so letting the\n// identical label reflow at (up to) the container's own width almost always drops it to one\n// line, which needs LESS height than Mermaid's original wrap — never more. That means this can\n// only ever shrink the label's footprint, never grow it, so no other node/edge/container ever\n// needs to move to make room. Verified headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names,\n// container widths from ~230px to ~1100px, wraps from 2 to 3 lines): every case converged to one\n// line with the same healthy negative gap a short, never-wrapped label already has; every\n// already-fits-on-one-line label (including every task in the golden `hello-guardrails` example)\n// was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\nfunction fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl) {\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n    const fo = label.querySelector('foreignObject');\n    const div = fo ? fo.querySelector('div') : null;\n    if (!fo || !div) continue;\n\n    const currentWidth = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('width')) || 0;\n    const currentHeight = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('height')) || 0;\n    if (currentWidth <= 0 || currentHeight <= 0) continue;\n\n    // scrollWidth/scrollHeight are LOCAL layout-box measurements in the foreignObject's own\n    // SVG-user-unit coordinate system — deliberately NOT the screen-space rect API (see class\n    // remarks): a screen-space read is affected by every ancestor SVG transform (dagre's per-node\n    // translate, the pan-zoom viewport's zoom/pan matrix), so it would be misleading compared\n    // against the foreignObject's own width/height attributes. Measure the label's natural\n    // single-line width by temporarily lifting the wrap constraint Mermaid applied, then restore\n    // it immediately.\n    const savedInline = div.getAttribute('style');\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    div.style.width = 'auto';\n    div.style.maxWidth = 'none';\n    // +2px safety buffer: scrollWidth can round down a hair short of the true subpixel width\n    // needed for one line (observed empirically — re-applying the exact measured value as a\n    // fixed width sometimes still wrapped to 2 lines by a fraction of a pixel).\n    const naturalWidth = div.scrollWidth + 2;\n    div.setAttribute('style', savedInline); // restore Mermaid's original wrapped styling\n\n    if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue; // already fits on one line — untouched\n\n    // Never widen past the cluster's own body (leave a small margin) — the container's leaf\n    // content already determined this width, so the label can use up to it without ever moving\n    // a leaf node, edge, or sibling container. Never NARROWER than Mermaid's original width either\n    // — this only ever grows the box.\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const newWidth = Math.min(naturalWidth, Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16));\n\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'break-spaces';\n    div.style.display = 'table';\n    div.style.width = newWidth + 'px';\n    div.style.maxWidth = newWidth + 'px';\n    const newHeight = div.scrollHeight;\n\n    if (newHeight >= currentHeight) {\n      // Widening did not actually reduce the wrapped height (the cluster is too narrow to fit\n      // even one more character per line) — revert rather than risk an oddly-proportioned label.\n      div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    fo.setAttribute('width', String(newWidth));\n    fo.setAttribute('height', String(newHeight));\n\n    // Mermaid centers the label group on the cluster's horizontal midpoint via\n    // `translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y)`; widening the box without re-centering would shift it\n    // left of center, so shift the existing translate by half the width delta to keep it on the\n    // SAME midpoint. The label's y stays fixed — only its height shrank, so its bottom edge\n    // simply moves UP, further from the first leaf node, never displacing it.\n    const transform = label.getAttribute('transform') || '';\n    const match = transform.match(/translate\\(([-\\d.eE]+)\\s*,\\s*([-\\d.eE]+)\\)/);\n    if (match) {\n      const oldX = parseFloat(match[1]);\n      const deltaCenter = (newWidth - currentWidth) / 2;\n      label.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${oldX - deltaCenter}, ${match[2]})`);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Inject a real clickable overlay on each task container's TITLE/LABEL ROW (issue #232/#233\n// superseded, issue #235). Mermaid never fires a `click` directive on a subgraph/cluster element,\n// and an anchor NODE inside the container gets packed into whatever sliver of space dagre's own\n// layout leaves — useless for a content-dense container. The title band is different: Mermaid\n// ALWAYS renders a cluster as exactly two children, a background <rect> then a <g\n// class=\"cluster-label\">, with the label in its own reserved header strip above any leaf content —\n// so a full-width band from the cluster's top down to just past the label's bottom edge is empty BY\n// CONSTRUCTION, regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has. Must run AFTER\n// fixWrappedClusterLabels (above): the band height is measured from the label's CURRENT bbox, so\n// a label that fixWrappedClusterLabels already shrank back to one line gets a correspondingly\n// short band, not one sized for its original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\nfunction addTaskContainerOverlays(svgEl) {\n  const ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const target = taskFolderTargets[cluster.id];\n    if (!target) continue; // not a task container (e.g. plan_preflights/plan_guardrails), or no map entry\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const labelBox = label.getBBox();\n    const bandHeight = (labelBox.y + labelBox.height) - clusterBox.y + 8; // small padding below the title\n\n    const a = document.createElementNS(ns, 'a');\n    a.setAttribute('href', target);\n    a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');\n    a.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open task folder: ' + target);\n\n    const rect = document.createElementNS(ns, 'rect');\n    rect.setAttribute('x', String(clusterBox.x));\n    rect.setAttribute('y', String(clusterBox.y));\n    rect.setAttribute('width', String(clusterBox.width));\n    rect.setAttribute('height', String(bandHeight));\n    // Inline style (not the `fill` ATTRIBUTE) deliberately: Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n    // carries a rule like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}` that colors every cluster's\n    // background rect. Since this overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group (so it stays in\n    // the same paint context as the background rect it sits atop), that same selector matches it\n    // too — and a CSS class/tag selector beats a plain presentation attribute, so `fill=\"transparent\"`\n    // as an attribute got silently overridden, painting a solid theme-colored bar over the title text.\n    // An inline style wins over any external/embedded stylesheet rule (short of `!important`), so it\n    // reliably stays invisible regardless of Mermaid's theme.\n    rect.style.fill = 'transparent';\n    rect.style.cursor = 'pointer';\n\n    a.appendChild(rect);\n    // Append as the LAST child — do NOT prepend as the first child. A cluster's only two original\n    // children are its background <rect> then its .cluster-label group (in that paint order).\n    // Appending puts the overlay on top of the background rect (so it is actually clickable)\n    // without covering the label text visually (the rect is transparent either way) — prepending\n    // instead would put the overlay BEHIND the background rect (which becomes second-in-order and\n    // paints over it), silently blocking every click.\n    cluster.appendChild(a);\n  }\n}\n\nlet pz = null;\ntry {\n  const { svg } = await mermaid.render('dag', graph);\n  document.getElementById('stage').innerHTML = svg;\n  const el = document.querySelector('#stage svg');\n  el.setAttribute('width', '100vw');\n  el.setAttribute('height', '100vh');\n  fixWrappedClusterLabels(el);\n  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\n  pz = svgPanZoom(el, { zoomEnabled: true, controlIconsEnabled: false, fit: true, center: true,\n                        minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\n  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\n} catch (e) {\n  // Surface the actual failure (offline CDN, or a Mermaid limit we have not yet lifted) instead of\n  // guessing — a generic \"offline?\" message sent every big-plan #108 failure down the wrong path.\n  const detail = (e && e.message) ? String(e.message) : String(e);\n  const p = document.createElement('p');\n  p.style.padding = '1rem';\n  p.textContent = 'Could not render the diagram: ' + detail +\n    ' — the DAG source is embedded in this page, and diagram.md renders on GitHub.';\n  const stage = document.getElementById('stage');\n  stage.innerHTML = '';\n  stage.appendChild(p);\n}\n\ndocument.getElementById('fit').onclick  = () => { if (pz) { pz.fit(); pz.center(); } };\ndocument.getElementById('zin').onclick  = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(1.3); };\ndocument.getElementById('zout').onclick = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(0.77); };\ndocument.getElementById('fs').onclick   = () => document.documentElement.requestFullscreen();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n\"\"\";\n}\n","numLines":394,"startLine":1,"totalLines":394}}}
