drag = pan &middot; Fit resets &middot; Fullscreen (or press F11).\n  Node clicks open source files &mdash; serve via a local HTTP server (e.g.\n  <code>python -m http.server</code>) for clicks to work; browsers block\n  <code>file://&rarr;file://</code> navigation by default.\n  On GitHub, diagram.md renders instead.</div>\n\n<script type=\"text/plain\" id=\"graph-source\">__GRAPH_SOURCE__</script>\n<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"task-folder-targets\">__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__</script>\n<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"search-index\">__SEARCH_INDEX__</script>\n<script src=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js\"></script>\n<script type=\"module\">\nimport mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';\n\nconst graph = document.getElementById('graph-source').textContent;\nconst taskFolderTargets = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('task-folder-targets').textContent);\nconst searchIndex = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('search-index').textContent);\n// securityLevel 'loose' is required for the `click ... href` directives to open node sources;\n// the content is the user's own local plan, served from file:// — not untrusted input.\n// maxTextSize raises Mermaid's default 50 000-character source ceiling (issue #108): a large\n// plan's DAG source easily exceeds it, and on overflow mermaid.render throws \"Maximum text size\n// in diagram exceeded\" — landing every big plan in the catch-block \"could not render\" fallback.\n// 5 000 000 covers DAGs far larger than any hand-reviewed plan while still bounding the parser.\n// maxEdges raises Mermaid's default 500-edge ceiling for the same reason: a many-task plan fans\n// out task→guardrail→done→dependent edges well past 500, and overflow throws \"Maximum number of\n// edges exceeded\". Both ceilings must be lifted or a big plan still fails to render.\nmermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'loose', maxTextSize: 5000000, maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: { useMaxWidth: false } });\n\n// Widen a wrapped cluster-title's foreignObject so a long kebab-case task name reflows onto\n// FEWER lines instead of overflowing Mermaid's fixed header-strip reservation (issue\n// cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Root cause, confirmed against the bundled mermaid@11.4.1 source\n// (`src/rendering-util/createText.ts`'s `createText(el, text, { width = 200 })` default, which\n// the plain flowchart \"rect\" cluster shape never overrides): a cluster's title <div> is always\n// wrapped to a hardcoded 200px width regardless of the container's own — usually much wider —\n// computed width, and dagre's LAYOUT PASS reserves header space for the container BEFORE that\n// wrapped height is known, so it never grows to fit more than a couple of lines. A short label\n// fits on one line inside 200px with room to spare (a healthy ~13px gap above the first leaf\n// node, measured); a long name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) wraps to 2 or more\n// lines, and each line beyond the first prints a full line-height PAST what dagre reserved —\n// landing on top of the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned directly below.\n//\n// Two Mermaid config knobs were checked and ruled out first: `flowchart.htmlLabels` only toggles\n// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer (not label width), and 11.4.1 has no documented\n// `flowchart`/theme-variable option for cluster-label wrapping width — 200 is a hardcoded\n// parameter default the cluster-shape renderer never overrides, not a configurable value.\n//\n// The fix instead re-wraps the SAME text into fewer lines post-render: a task container is\n// normally already wider than 200px (dagre sized it to fit its leaf content), so letting the\n// identical label reflow at (up to) the container's own width almost always drops it to one\n// line, which needs LESS height than Mermaid's original wrap — never more. That means this can\n// only ever shrink the label's footprint, never grow it, so no other node/edge/container ever\n// needs to move to make room. Verified headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names,\n// container widths from ~230px to ~1100px, wraps from 2 to 3 lines): every case converged to one\n// line with the same healthy negative gap a short, never-wrapped label already has; every\n// already-fits-on-one-line label (including every task in the golden `hello-guardrails` example)\n// was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\nfunction fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl) {\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n    const fo = label.querySelector('foreignObject');\n    const div = fo ? fo.querySelector('div') : null;\n    if (!fo || !div) continue;\n\n    const currentWidth = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('width')) || 0;\n    const currentHeight = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('height')) || 0;\n    if (currentWidth <= 0 || currentHeight <= 0) continue;\n\n    // scrollWidth/scrollHeight are LOCAL layout-box measurements in the foreignObject's own\n    // SVG-user-unit coordinate system — deliberately NOT the screen-space rect API (see class\n    // remarks): a screen-space read is affected by every ancestor SVG transform (dagre's per-node\n    // translate, the pan-zoom viewport's zoom/pan matrix), so it would be misleading compared\n    // against the foreignObject's own width/height attributes. Measure the label's natural\n    // single-line width by temporarily lifting the wrap constraint Mermaid applied, then restore\n    // it immediately.\n    const savedInline = div.getAttribute('style');\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    div.style.width = 'auto';\n    div.style.maxWidth = 'none';\n    // +2px safety buffer: scrollWidth can round down a hair short of the true subpixel width\n    // needed for one line (observed empirically — re-applying the exact measured value as a\n    // fixed width sometimes still wrapped to 2 lines by a fraction of a pixel).\n    const naturalWidth = div.scrollWidth + 2;\n    div.setAttribute('style', savedInline); // restore Mermaid's original wrapped styling\n\n    if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue; // already fits on one line — untouched\n\n    // Never widen past the cluster's own body (leave a small margin) — the container's leaf\n    // content already determined this width, so the label can use up to it without ever moving\n    // a leaf node, edge, or sibling container. Never NARROWER than Mermaid's original width either\n    // — this only ever grows the box.\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const newWidth = Math.min(naturalWidth, Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16));\n\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'break-spaces';\n    div.style.display = 'table';\n    div.style.width = newWidth + 'px';\n    div.style.maxWidth = newWidth + 'px';\n    const newHeight = div.scrollHeight;\n\n    if (newHeight >= currentHeight) {\n      // Widening did not actually reduce the wrapped height (the cluster is too narrow to fit\n      // even one more character per line) — revert rather than risk an oddly-proportioned label.\n      div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    fo.setAttribute('width', String(newWidth));\n    fo.setAttribute('height', String(newHeight));\n\n    // Mermaid centers the label group on the cluster's horizontal midpoint via\n    // `translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y)`; widening the box without re-centering would shift it\n    // left of center, so shift the existing translate by half the width delta to keep it on the\n    // SAME midpoint. The label's y stays fixed — only its height shrank, so its bottom edge\n    // simply moves UP, further from the first leaf node, never displacing it.\n    const transform = label.getAttribute('transform') || '';\n    const match = transform.match(/translate\\(([-\\d.eE]+)\\s*,\\s*([-\\d.eE]+)\\)/);\n    if (match) {\n      const oldX = parseFloat(match[1]);\n      const deltaCenter = (newWidth - currentWidth) / 2;\n      label.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${oldX - deltaCenter}, ${match[2]})`);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Inject a real clickable overlay on each task container's TITLE/LABEL ROW (issue #232/#233\n// superseded, issue #235). Mermaid never fires a `click` directive on a subgraph/cluster element,\n// and an anchor NODE inside the container gets packed into whatever sliver of space dagre's own\n// layout leaves — useless for a content-dense container. The title band is different: Mermaid\n// ALWAYS renders a cluster as exactly two children, a background <rect> then a <g\n// class=\"cluster-label\">, with the label in its own reserved header strip above any leaf content —\n// so a full-width band from the cluster's top down to just past the label's bottom edge is empty BY\n// CONSTRUCTION, regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has. Must run AFTER\n// fixWrappedClusterLabels (above): the band height is measured from the label's CURRENT bbox, so\n// a label that fixWrappedClusterLabels already shrank back to one line gets a correspondingly\n// short band, not one sized for its original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\nfunction addTaskContainerOverlays(svgEl) {\n  const ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const target = taskFolderTargets[cluster.id];\n    if (!target) continue; // not a task container (e.g. plan_preflights/plan_guardrails), or no map entry\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const labelBox = label.getBBox();\n    const bandHeight = (labelBox.y + labelBox.height) - clusterBox.y + 8; // small padding below the title\n\n    const a = document.createElementNS(ns, 'a');\n    a.setAttribute('href', target);\n    a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');\n    a.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open task folder: ' + target);\n\n    const rect = document.createElementNS(ns, 'rect');\n    rect.setAttribute('x', String(clusterBox.x));\n    rect.setAttribute('y', String(clusterBox.y));\n    rect.setAttribute('width', String(clusterBox.width));\n    rect.setAttribute('height', String(bandHeight));\n    // Inline style (not the `fill` ATTRIBUTE) deliberately: Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n    // carries a rule like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}` that colors every cluster's\n    // background rect. Since this overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group (so it stays in\n    // the same paint context as the background rect it sits atop), that same selector matches it\n    // too — and a CSS class/tag selector beats a plain presentation attribute, so `fill=\"transparent\"`\n    // as an attribute got silently overridden, painting a solid theme-colored bar over the title text.\n    // An inline style wins over any external/embedded stylesheet rule (short of `!important`), so it\n    // reliably stays invisible regardless of Mermaid's theme.\n    rect.style.fill = 'transparent';\n    rect.style.cursor = 'pointer';\n\n    a.appendChild(rect);\n    // Append as the LAST child — do NOT prepend as the first child. A cluster's only two original\n    // children are its background <rect> then its .cluster-label group (in that paint order).\n    // Appending puts the overlay on top of the background rect (so it is actually clickable)\n    // without covering the label text visually (the rect is transparent either way) — prepending\n    // instead would put the overlay BEHIND the background rect (which becomes second-in-order and\n    // paints over it), silently blocking every click.\n    cluster.appendChild(a);\n  }\n}\n\n// Diagram search (issue #220): substring-matches the typed query (case-insensitive) against every\n// entry in `searchIndex` (id -> visible label, built by BuildSearchIndexJson — see class remarks),\n// toggles each matching node's class to 'search-match' and every other node's to 'search-dim' (pure\n// class toggling, no Mermaid re-render), updates the \"N of M\" counter, and auto pans/zooms the FIRST\n// match into view via the SAME pan-zoom instance API positionStatusBadges' overlay already uses:\n// pz.getPan(), pz.getSizes(), pz.pan({ x, y }), pz.zoom(z).\n// STUB (deliberate TDD red — see BuildSearchIndexJson): searchIndex is always empty until\n// 08-implement-diagram-search-box lands the real parsing, so this never has real work to do yet.\nfunction runSearch(query) {\n  throw new Error('NotImplementedException: diagram search (issue #220) is not implemented yet');\n}\n\nlet pz = null;\ntry {\n  const { svg } = await mermaid.render('dag', graph);\n  document.getElementById('stage').innerHTML = svg;\n  const el = document.querySelector('#stage svg');\n  el.setAttribute('width', '100vw');\n  el.setAttribute('height', '100vh');\n  fixWrappedClusterLabels(el);\n  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\n  pz = svgPanZoom(el, { zoomEnabled: true, controlIconsEnabled: false, fit: true, center: true,\n                        minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\n  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\n} catch (e) {\n  // Surface the actual failure (offline CDN, or a Mermaid limit we have not yet lifted) instead of\n  // guessing — a generic \"offline?\" message sent every big-plan #108 failure down the wrong path.\n  const detail = (e && e.message) ? String(e.message) : String(e);\n  const p = document.createElement('p');\n  p.style.padding = '1rem';\n  p.textContent = 'Could not render the diagram: ' + detail +\n    ' — the DAG source is embedded in this page, and diagram.md renders on GitHub.';\n  const stage = document.getElementById('stage');\n  stage.innerHTML = '';\n  stage.appendChild(p);\n}\n\ndocument.getElementById('fit').onclick  = () => { if (pz) { pz.fit(); pz.center(); } };\ndocument.getElementById('zin').onclick  = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(1.3); };\ndocument.getElementById('zout').onclick = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(0.77); };\ndocument.getElementById('fs').onclick   = () => document.documentElement.requestFullscreen();\n\ndocument.getElementById('search-input').addEventListener('input', (e) => runSearch(e.target.value));\ndocument.getElementById('search-prev').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\ndocument.getElementById('search-next').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n\"\"\";\n}\n","numLines":670,"startLine":1,"totalLines":670}}}

It WRAPS the real observer (live <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> or\n10\t/// <see cref=\"ConsoleRunObserver\"/>), forwards every event verbatim, and AFTER forwarding rewrites\n11\t/// the site through <see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer\"/>:\n12\t/// <list type=\"bullet\">\n13\t///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskStarting\"/> a task flips pending → running and the index is rewritten —\n14\t///     a running task links to the LIVE server (a click tails it) when a server is up, else plain text.</item>\n15\t///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskFinished\"/> a task flips to its settled status, its static page is written\n16\t///     (<see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts\"/>), and the index is rewritten — a\n17\t///     settled task with attempts on disk now links to its static page.</item>\n18\t/// </list>\n19\t///\n20\t/// <para>The index always carries the <c>meta refresh</c> (<c>includeRefresh:true</c>) so a\n21\t/// <c>file://</c> view re-reads it as it is rewritten; the DURABLE final/<c>--export</c> index (no\n22\t/// refresh, all-static) is written separately by the run's end-of-run path, NOT here.</para>\n23\t///\n24\t/// <para>The renderer writes atomically, so a browser never reads a torn file. This decorator's own\n25\t/// status map is the only shared mutable state, and M4 worker threads call in concurrently, so all\n26\t/// access to it — and the write that projects from it — is serialised under one lock. Renders are\n27\t/// best-effort: a render failure (e.g. a transient file lock) is swallowed so a UX nicety never\n28\t/// flips a task's outcome or aborts the run.</para>\n29\t/// </summary>\n30\tpublic sealed class OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver : IRunObserver\n31\t{\n32\t    private readonly IRunObserver _inner;\n33\t    private readonly string _logsRoot;\n34\t    private readonly string _runId;\n35\t    private readonly IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> _tasks;\n36\t    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TaskNode> _tasksById;\n37\t    private readonly Func<string, string?>? _liveUrlForTask;\n38\t\n39\t    // Per-task status word, seeded \"pending\". Mutated and projected under one lock — events arrive\n40\t    // from concurrent M4 workers, and the index render reads the whole map, so the two must not race.\n41\t    private readonly object _gate = new();\n42\t    private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _statusByTask;\n43\t\n44\t    /// <param name=\"inner\">The real observer every event is forwarded to (live or console).</param>\n45\t    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the site is written into.</param>\n46\t    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n47\t    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n48\t    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">\n49\t    /// Resolver mapping a task id to its live-server URL, or null when no server is up. A RUNNING task\n50\t    /// links to this URL (a click tails it) when non-null; null = the running task is plain text.\n51\t    /// </param>\n52\t    public OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver(\n53\t        IRunObserver inner,\n54\t        string logsRoot,\n55\t        string runId,\n56\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n57\t        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n58\t    {\n59\t        _inner = inner ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(inner));\n60\t        _logsRoot = logsRoot;\n61\t        _runId = runId;\n62\t        _tasks = tasks;\n63\t        _tasksById = tasks.ToDictionary(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n64\t        _liveUrlForTask = liveUrlForTask;\n65\t        _statusByTask = tasks.ToDictionary(\n66\t            t => t.Id, _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending), StringComparer.Ordinal);\n67\t    }\n68\t\n69\t    /// <summary>\n70\t    /// Write the initial all-pending index at run start (every task pending, plain text), so the \"all\n71\t    /// tasks\" page exists and is browsable the moment the run begins. Best-effort. Delegates to the\n72\t    /// static <see cref=\"WriteInitialIndex(string, string, IReadOnlyList{TaskNode}, Func{string, string?})\"/>.\n73\t    /// </summary>\n74\t    public void WriteInitialIndex() => WriteInitialIndex(_logsRoot, _runId, _tasks, _liveUrlForTask);\n75\t\n76\t    /// <summary>\n77\t    /// Write the initial all-pending index (every task <c>pending</c>, plain link, with the during-run\n78\t    /// meta-refresh) WITHOUT an observer instance, so the live path can write it — and print the\n79\t    /// link to it — BEFORE constructing <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> (which starts the Spectre\n80\t    /// <c>AnsiConsole.Live</c> region in its ctor). Any console write into an active Live region\n81\t    /// corrupts the table, so the initial index + its static-index link must be emitted first (#145\n82\t    /// Bug 1). Best-effort: a render failure is swallowed (a UX nicety never aborts the run).\n83\t    /// </summary>\n84\t    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the index is written into.</param>\n85\t    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n86\t    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n87\t    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">Unused at the all-pending start (no task is running yet); accepted\n88\t    /// so the static signature matches the instance's link-resolution surface for callers.</param>\n89\t    public static void WriteInitialIndex(\n90\t        string logsRoot,\n91\t        string runId,\n92\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n93\t        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n94\t    {\n95\t        _ = liveUrlForTask; // no task is running at the all-pending start, so no live link is resolved yet\n96\t        string pending = LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending);\n97\t        TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n98\t            logsRoot,\n99\t            runId,\n100\t            tasks,\n101\t            statusResolver: _ => pending,\n102\t            linkResolver: _ => LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain,\n103\t            includeRefresh: true));\n104\t    }\n105\t\n106\t    public void TaskStarting(TaskNode task)\n107\t    {\n108\t        _inner.TaskStarting(task);\n109\t        SetStatus(task.Id, LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running));\n110\t        RenderIndex();\n111\t    }\n112\t\n113\t    public void AttemptStarting(TaskNode task, int attempt, int budget) =>\n114\t        _inner.AttemptStarting(task, attempt, budget);\n115\t\n116\t    public void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result) =>\n117\t        _inner.GuardrailFinished(task, result);\n118\t\n119\t    public void TaskFinished(TaskResult result)\n120\t    {\n121\t        _inner.TaskFinished(result);\n122\t        SetStatus(result.TaskId, StatusWord(result.Outcome));\n123\t\n124\t        // Write the finished task's static page so the index's link to it (and the terminal's\n125\t        // post-mortem link, #141 item 1) resolves to a rendered page, not a 404.\n126\t        if (_tasksById.TryGetValue(result.TaskId, out TaskNode? task))\n127\t        {\n128\t            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts(_logsRoot, task));\n129\t        }\n130\t\n131\t        RenderIndex();\n132\t    }\n133\t\n134\t    public void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) => _inner.PlanHashMismatch(previousPlanHash);\n135\t\n136\t    public void ParallelismClampedNoProvider(int requested) => _inner.ParallelismClampedNoProvider(requested);\n137\t\n138\t    public void CleanupFailed(string owner, Exception error) => _inner.CleanupFailed(owner, error);\n139\t\n140\t    public void PromptPaused(TaskNode task, string reason, TimeSpan backoff, int pauseCount) =>\n141\t        _inner.PromptPaused(task, reason, backoff, pauseCount);\n142\t\n143\t    // --- site projection --------------------------------------------------------------------\n144\t\n145\t    private void SetStatus(string taskId, string status)\n146\t    {\n147\t        lock (_gate)\n148\t        {\n149\t            _statusByTask[taskId] = status;\n150\t        }\n151\t    }\n152\t\n153\t    /// <summary>\n154\t    /// Rewrite the during-run index (with refresh) from the current status map. Holds the lock for the\n155\t    /// whole render so the status snapshot and the link choice are consistent (the renderer writes\n156\t    /// atomically). The link resolver: a RUNNING task → the live URL when a server is up (else plain),\n157\t    /// any task with attempts on disk → its static page, anything else → plain text.\n158\t    /// </summary>\n159\t    private void RenderIndex()\n160\t    {\n161\t        lock (_gate)\n162\t        {\n163\t            // Snapshot the statuses inside the lock so the resolver closures read a stable view.\n164\t            var statuses = new Dictionary<string, string>(_statusByTask, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n165\t            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n166\t                _logsRoot,\n167\t                _runId,\n168\t                _tasks,\n169\t                statusResolver: id => statuses.TryGetValue(id, out string? s) ? s : \"unknown\",\n170\t                linkResolver: id => ResolveLink(id, statuses),\n171\t                includeRefresh: true));\n172\t        }\n173\t    }\n174\t\n175\t    private LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink ResolveLink(string taskId, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> statuses)\n176\t    {\n177\t        bool running = statuses.TryGetValue(taskId, out string? status) &&\n178\t                       status == LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running);\n179\t\n180\t        // A running task links to the live server (a click tails it) when one is up; otherwise it is\n181\t        // plain text (no static page to point at yet).\n182\t        if (running && _liveUrlForTask?.Invoke(taskId) is { } liveUrl)\n183\t        {\n184\t            return LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.LiveTo(liveUrl);\n185\t        }\n186\t\n187\t        // A task with attempts on disk (running-without-server, or settled) links to its static page;\n188\t        // a pending/no-attempt task is plain text.\n189\t        return HasAttempts(taskId) ? LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Static : LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain;\n190\t    }\n191\t\n192\t    private bool HasAttempts(string taskId)\n193\t    {\n194\t        string taskDir = Path.Combine(_logsRoot, taskId);\n195\t        if (!Directory.Exists(taskDir))\n196\t        {\n197\t            return false;\n198\t        }\n199\t\n200\t        return Directory.EnumerateDirectories(taskDir)\n201\t            .Any(d => Path.GetFileName(d).StartsWith(\"attempt-\", StringComparison.Ordinal));\n202\t    }\n203\t\n204\t    /// <summary>Map a finished task's outcome to the index status word (mirrors the journal mapping).</summary>\n205\t    private static string StatusWord(TaskOutcome outcome) => outcome switch\n206\t    {\n207\t        TaskOutcome.Succeeded => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Succeeded),\n208\t        TaskOutcome.Skipped => \"skipped\",\n209\t        TaskOutcome.Blocked => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Blocked),\n210\t        TaskOutcome.Cancelled => \"cancelled\",\n211\t        // ActionFailed / GuardrailFailed / InvalidFragment / NeedsHuman are all needs-human terminal.\n212\t        _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.NeedsHuman),\n213\t    };\n214\t\n215\t    /// <summary>\n216\t    /// Run a render action, swallowing IO failures: the on-the-fly site is a UX nicety and must never\n217\t    /// flip a task's outcome or abort the run. A transient lock/torn-read is retried by the next event.\n218\t    /// </summary>\n219\t    private static void TryRender(Action render)\n220\t    {\n221\t        try\n222\t        {\n223\t            render();\n224\t        }\n225\t        catch (IOException)\n226\t        {\n227\t            // best-effort — the next event re-renders\n228\t        }\n229\t        catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)\n230\t        {\n231\t            // best-effort — never let a logs-tree permission hiccup abort the run\n232\t        }\n233\t    }\n234\t}\n235\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"da2e2042-c4b6-4ef5-b6ac-18dee996d70e","uuid":"28299401-f0ce-4d92-a176-dc4620505a6c","timestamp":"2026-07-07T17:11:25.286Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"src\\Guardrails.Cli\\Ui\\OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver.cs","content":"using Guardrails.Core.Execution;\nusing Guardrails.Core.Model;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Cli.Ui;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// A decorator <see cref=\"IRunObserver\"/> that keeps the DURING-RUN static log site\n/// (<c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/index.html</c> + per-task pages) up to date as the run proceeds (issue #141\n/// item 2). It WRAPS the real observer (live <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> or\n/// <see cref=\"ConsoleRunObserver\"/>), forwards every event verbatim, and AFTER forwarding rewrites\n/// the site through <see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer\"/>:\n/// <list type=\"bullet\">\n///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskStarting\"/> a task flips pending → running and the index is rewritten —\n///     a running task links to the LIVE server (a click tails it) when a server is up, else plain text.</item>\n///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskFinished\"/> a task flips to its settled status, its static page is written\n///     (<see cref=\"LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts\"/>), and the index is rewritten — a\n///     settled task with attempts on disk now links to its static page.</item>\n/// </list>\n///\n/// <para>The index always carries the <c>meta refresh</c> (<c>includeRefresh:true</c>) so a\n/// <c>file://</c> view re-reads it as it is rewritten; the DURABLE final/<c>--export</c> index (no\n/// refresh, all-static) is written separately by the run's end-of-run path, NOT here.</para>\n///\n/// <para>The renderer writes atomically, so a browser never reads a torn file. This decorator's own\n/// status map is the only shared mutable state, and M4 worker threads call in concurrently, so all\n/// access to it — and the write that projects from it — is serialised under one lock. Renders are\n/// best-effort: a render failure (e.g. a transient file lock) is swallowed so a UX nicety never\n/// flips a task's outcome or aborts the run.</para>\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver : IRunObserver\n{\n    private readonly IRunObserver _inner;\n    private readonly string _logsRoot;\n    private readonly string _runId;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> _tasks;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TaskNode> _tasksById;\n    private readonly Func<string, string?>? _liveUrlForTask;\n\n    // Per-task status word, seeded \"pending\". Mutated and projected under one lock — events arrive\n    // from concurrent M4 workers, and the index render reads the whole map, so the two must not race.\n    private readonly object _gate = new();\n    private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _statusByTask;\n\n    /// <param name=\"inner\">The real observer every event is forwarded to (live or console).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the site is written into.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">\n    /// Resolver mapping a task id to its live-server URL, or null when no server is up. A RUNNING task\n    /// links to this URL (a click tails it) when non-null; null = the running task is plain text.\n    /// </param>\n    public OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver(\n        IRunObserver inner,\n        string logsRoot,\n        string runId,\n        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n    {\n        _inner = inner ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(inner));\n        _logsRoot = logsRoot;\n        _runId = runId;\n        _tasks = tasks;\n        _tasksById = tasks.ToDictionary(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n        _liveUrlForTask = liveUrlForTask;\n        _statusByTask = tasks.ToDictionary(\n            t => t.Id, _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending), StringComparer.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Write the initial all-pending index at run start (every task pending, plain text), so the \"all\n    /// tasks\" page exists and is browsable the moment the run begins. Best-effort. Delegates to the\n    /// static <see cref=\"WriteInitialIndex(string, string, IReadOnlyList{TaskNode}, Func{string, string?})\"/>.\n    /// </summary>\n    public void WriteInitialIndex() => WriteInitialIndex(_logsRoot, _runId, _tasks, _liveUrlForTask);\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Write the initial all-pending index (every task <c>pending</c>, plain link, with the during-run\n    /// meta-refresh) WITHOUT an observer instance, so the live path can write it — and print the\n    /// link to it — BEFORE constructing <see cref=\"LiveRunObserver\"/> (which starts the Spectre\n    /// <c>AnsiConsole.Live</c> region in its ctor). Any console write into an active Live region\n    /// corrupts the table, so the initial index + its static-index link must be emitted first (#145\n    /// Bug 1). Best-effort: a render failure is swallowed (a UX nicety never aborts the run).\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <param name=\"logsRoot\">The run's <c>logs/&lt;runId&gt;/</c> tree the index is written into.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"runId\">The run id (titles the rendered index).</param>\n    /// <param name=\"tasks\">The plan's tasks, in plan order — the rows of the index.</param>\n    /// <param name=\"liveUrlForTask\">Unused at the all-pending start (no task is running yet); accepted\n    /// so the static signature matches the instance's link-resolution surface for callers.</param>\n    public static void WriteInitialIndex(\n        string logsRoot,\n        string runId,\n        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n        Func<string, string?>? liveUrlForTask)\n    {\n        _ = liveUrlForTask; // no task is running at the all-pending start, so no live link is resolved yet\n        string pending = LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Pending);\n        TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n            logsRoot,\n            runId,\n            tasks,\n            statusResolver: _ => pending,\n            linkResolver: _ => LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain,\n            includeRefresh: true));\n    }\n\n    public void TaskStarting(TaskNode task)\n    {\n        _inner.TaskStarting(task);\n        SetStatus(task.Id, LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running));\n        RenderIndex();\n    }\n\n    public void AttemptStarting(TaskNode task, int attempt, int budget) =>\n        _inner.AttemptStarting(task, attempt, budget);\n\n    public void GuardrailFinished(TaskNode task, GuardrailResult result) =>\n        _inner.GuardrailFinished(task, result);\n\n    public void TaskFinished(TaskResult result)\n    {\n        _inner.TaskFinished(result);\n        SetStatus(result.TaskId, StatusWord(result.Outcome));\n\n        // Write the finished task's static page so the index's link to it (and the terminal's\n        // post-mortem link, #141 item 1) resolves to a rendered page, not a 404.\n        if (_tasksById.TryGetValue(result.TaskId, out TaskNode? task))\n        {\n            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteTaskPageIfHasAttempts(_logsRoot, task));\n        }\n\n        RenderIndex();\n    }\n\n    public void PlanHashMismatch(string previousPlanHash) => _inner.PlanHashMismatch(previousPlanHash);\n\n    public void ParallelismClampedNoProvider(int requested) => _inner.ParallelismClampedNoProvider(requested);\n\n    public void CleanupFailed(string owner, Exception error) => _inner.CleanupFailed(owner, error);\n\n    public void PromptPaused(TaskNode task, string reason, TimeSpan backoff, int pauseCount) =>\n        _inner.PromptPaused(task, reason, backoff, pauseCount);\n\n    // --- site projection --------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    private void SetStatus(string taskId, string status)\n    {\n        lock (_gate)\n        {\n            _statusByTask[taskId] = status;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Rewrite the during-run index (with refresh) from the current status map. Holds the lock for the\n    /// whole render so the status snapshot and the link choice are consistent (the renderer writes\n    /// atomically). The link resolver: a RUNNING task → the live URL when a server is up (else plain),\n    /// any task with attempts on disk → its static page, anything else → plain text.\n    /// </summary>\n    private void RenderIndex()\n    {\n        lock (_gate)\n        {\n            // Snapshot the statuses inside the lock so the resolver closures read a stable view.\n            var statuses = new Dictionary<string, string>(_statusByTask, StringComparer.Ordinal);\n            TryRender(() => LogSiteRenderer.WriteIndex(\n                _logsRoot,\n                _runId,\n                _tasks,\n                statusResolver: id => statuses.TryGetValue(id, out string? s) ? s : \"unknown\",\n                linkResolver: id => ResolveLink(id, statuses),\n                includeRefresh: true));\n        }\n    }\n\n    private LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink ResolveLink(string taskId, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> statuses)\n    {\n        bool running = statuses.TryGetValue(taskId, out string? status) &&\n                       status == LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Running);\n\n        // A running task links to the live server (a click tails it) when one is up; otherwise it is\n        // plain text (no static page to point at yet).\n        if (running && _liveUrlForTask?.Invoke(taskId) is { } liveUrl)\n        {\n            return LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.LiveTo(liveUrl);\n        }\n\n        // A task with attempts on disk (running-without-server, or settled) links to its static page;\n        // a pending/no-attempt task is plain text.\n        return HasAttempts(taskId) ? LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Static : LogSiteRenderer.IndexLink.Plain;\n    }\n\n    private bool HasAttempts(string taskId)\n    {\n        string taskDir = Path.Combine(_logsRoot, taskId);\n        if (!Directory.Exists(taskDir))\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        return Directory.EnumerateDirectories(taskDir)\n            .Any(d => Path.GetFileName(d).StartsWith(\"attempt-\", StringComparison.Ordinal));\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Map a finished task's outcome to the index status word (mirrors the journal mapping).</summary>\n    private static string StatusWord(TaskOutcome outcome) => outcome switch\n    {\n        TaskOutcome.Succeeded => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Succeeded),\n        TaskOutcome.Skipped => \"skipped\",\n        TaskOutcome.Blocked => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.Blocked),\n        TaskOutcome.Cancelled => \"cancelled\",\n        // ActionFailed / GuardrailFailed / InvalidFragment / NeedsHuman are all needs-human terminal.\n        _ => LogSiteRenderer.StatusText(Core.Journal.TaskStatus.NeedsHuman),\n    };\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Run a render action, swallowing IO failures: the on-the-fly site is a UX nicety and must never\n    /// flip a task's outcome or abort the run. A transient lock/torn-read is retried by the next event.\n    /// </summary>\n    private static void TryRender(Action render)\n    {\n        try\n        {\n            render();\n        }\n        catch (IOException)\n        {\n            // best-effort — the next event re-renders\n        }\n        catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)\n        {\n            // best-effort — never let a logs-tree permission hiccup abort the run\n        }\n    }\n}\n","numLines":235,"startLine":1,"totalLines":235}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XReZcK6N64BwbK9WKRdVRP","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tusing System.Text;\n2\tusing Guardrails.Core.Model;\n3\t\n4\tnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n5\t\n6\t/// <summary>\n7\t/// Renders a plan's task/guardrail DAG as a Mermaid <c>flowchart TD</c> (SSOT §10) using the\n8\t/// CONTAINER model (design-of-record 09-preflight-first-class). Pure: <see cref=\"Render\"/> maps\n9\t/// a <see cref=\"PlanDefinition\"/> to Mermaid text with no I/O.\n10\t/// </summary>\n11\t/// <remarks>\n12\t/// <para>\n13\t/// Shape: each task is a <c>subgraph task_&lt;id&gt;</c> container holding its check nodes\n14\t/// (preflight and guardrail leaves) DIRECTLY inside the container — no nested\n15\t/// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph, no free guardrail/preflight nodes outside\n16\t/// a container, no per-task <c>done_&lt;id&gt;</c> reconvergence node, no <c>task --&gt; guardrail</c>\n17\t/// fan-out edge. (A per-task nested-subgraph wrapper was tried and dropped — see \"Nested boxes\n18\t/// dropped\" below.) Two mandatory plan-level containers bracket the whole DAG: <c>plan_preflights</c>\n19\t/// (\"Full Flight Checks\") at the top, <c>plan_guardrails</c> (\"Terminal Gate\") at the bottom —\n20\t/// always emitted, even when their folder is empty, because they are structural brackets, not\n21\t/// conditional content. These two stay titled subgraphs (unaffected by the nested-box removal\n22\t/// below): they are one-off heterogeneous brackets on the whole DAG, not a per-task repeated\n23\t/// pattern.\n24\t/// </para>\n25\t/// <para>\n26\t/// <b>Nested boxes dropped (simplification).</b> A task container previously nested a\n27\t/// \"Guardrails\" sub-container (and, when present, a \"Preflights\" sub-container) around its leaf\n28\t/// check nodes — nesting-within-nesting that made a real generated diagram look busy for no\n29\t/// semantic gain: the wrapper subgraph id was never referenced by edge emission, container\n30\t/// styling, or <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> — purely cosmetic. Leaf check nodes are now emitted\n31\t/// as direct children of the task container; the existing <c>:::preflight</c>/<c>:::guardrail</c>\n32\t/// <c>classDef</c> fill remains the only visual category distinction. Removing the boxes also\n33\t/// removes their visual \"preflights run before, guardrails run after\" cue, so that temporal fact\n34\t/// is now preserved two other ways: (1) a GUARANTEED emission-order contract — a task's preflight\n35\t/// leaf node(s), if any, are always emitted before its guardrail leaf node(s) within the\n36\t/// container (see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>), so position is a stable, tested convention,\n37\t/// not a rendering accident; and (2) the legend (see <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/>) states the\n38\t/// before/after timing in words, not just a bare colour-category name.\n39\t/// </para>\n40\t/// <para>\n41\t/// <b>Legend lives outside the Mermaid graph.</b> A Mermaid-native legend (a disconnected\n42\t/// subgraph of dummy colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN headless against the\n43\t/// exact bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>: dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra\n44\t/// \"task\" overlapping the real DAG. The only approach that renders correctly is content OUTSIDE\n45\t/// the Mermaid source entirely: an HTML overlay `&lt;div&gt;` in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>\n46\t/// for <c>diagram.html</c>, and the shared <see cref=\"LegendMarkdown\"/> block placed by the CLI's\n47\t/// <c>graph</c> command AFTER the fenced <c>```mermaid```</c> block for <c>diagram.md</c> (GitHub's\n48\t/// Mermaid sandbox has no overlay option). Neither destination is part of <see cref=\"Render\"/>'s or\n49\t/// <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>'s returned Mermaid source, and — same treatment as the existing\n50\t/// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> color lines (added by those two methods, never by\n51\t/// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>) — the legend never reaches <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> either,\n52\t/// so legend-only wording changes never move <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> and never make\n53\t/// `graph --check` spuriously report a plan stale.\n54\t/// </para>\n55\t/// <para>\n56\t/// <b>Every check node's drawn label is its short, stable <c>Name</c> — never its (possibly long)\n57\t/// <c>Description</c>.</b> A prior version drew a task-level preflight's full descriptive text\n58\t/// (which can run to many words) and truncated it to fit; the owner asked instead for the same\n59\t/// short, meaningful identifier the node's own click target already opens, uniformly for every\n60\t/// check kind at both scopes (issue #222) — so no truncation heuristic is needed anywhere. The\n61\t/// full <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/> remains reachable via the SAME\n62\t/// <c>click</c>-directive mechanism <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> already uses for every node\n63\t/// (source-file click-through, issue #33) — the tooltip argument of that directive carries the\n64\t/// full text for every check, so no new mechanism was introduced.\n65\t/// </para>\n66\t/// <para>\n67\t/// The DAG is drawn <c>subgraph --&gt; subgraph</c>: each edge references a container's subgraph\n68\t/// id directly (<c>task_A --&gt; task_B</c>, <c>plan_preflights --&gt; task_root</c>, …), so Mermaid\n69\t/// clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER like any ordinary box-to-box flowchart edge —\n70\t/// no interior anchor, no line piercing the box (issue #210). The bundled Mermaid version\n71\t/// (<c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>, CDN-pinned in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>) renders these\n72\t/// boundary-clipped subgraph edges faithfully; this was verified by rendering both the anchor\n73\t/// form and the direct form headless against 11.4.1 and measuring the edge endpoints (the anchor\n74\t/// form terminated ~65px INSIDE each box; the direct form lands ON the border). Container \"kind\"\n75\t/// styling (task / plan-level) is applied via a per-container <c>style &lt;id&gt; fill:…;</c>\n76\t/// statement rather than a <c>class &lt;id&gt; &lt;className&gt;;</c> assignment — in 11.4.1 a\n77\t/// <c>class</c> assignment does not reach a subgraph that is itself an edge endpoint (and every\n78\t/// container is one under the subgraph→subgraph model), whereas <c>style &lt;id&gt;</c> colours it\n79\t/// and also colours an EMPTY plan-level bracket (which Mermaid renders as a plain node, not a\n80\t/// cluster). Only the LEAF check nodes keep <c>classDef</c>-based colouring (<c>:::preflight</c> /\n81\t/// <c>:::guardrail</c>).\n82\t/// </para>\n83\t/// <para>\n84\t/// <b>A task container's click target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay on its title band (issue\n85\t/// #232/#233 superseded, issue #235), NOT a Mermaid-source mechanism at all.</b> The #210 edge fix\n86\t/// above only changed how DAG EDGES attach to a container; it did not change (and never claimed to\n87\t/// change) how the container's own click target resolves. Real headless-Chrome verification against\n88\t/// the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c> — clicking the container body, its title text, and its fill\n89\t/// rect, then checking whether a real navigation (a popup) actually fired — proved a Mermaid\n90\t/// <c>click</c> directive targeting a subgraph/cluster id NEVER fires: Mermaid wraps a clickable LEAF\n91\t/// node in a real <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c> element (confirmed firing), but never wraps a\n92\t/// <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster\"&gt;</c> (subgraph) in one, regardless of what id a <c>click</c> directive\n93\t/// names. This is a genuine, still-open upstream Mermaid limitation: mermaid-js/mermaid#1637 (\"Let\n94\t/// subgraph handle clicks\") and #5428 (\"click action for subgraphs\") are both open feature requests\n95\t/// as of this writing.\n96\t/// </para>\n97\t/// <para>\n98\t/// <b>Why the first fix (#232/#233, an invisible anchor NODE) was insufficient.</b> That fix added\n99\t/// one <c>{containerId}_anchor[\" \"]:::invisible</c> node per container and pointed the container's\n100\t/// <c>click</c> directive at it instead of the subgraph id — which DOES fire (Mermaid wraps it in a\n101\t/// real <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>, like any leaf node) but is USELESS in practice: dagre (Mermaid's layout\n102\t/// engine) sizes a <c>[\" \"]</c>-labelled node to a tiny default (~39×20px) and packs it wherever ITS\n103\t/// OWN layout algorithm decides — for a container with several guardrail leaf boxes packed\n104\t/// side-by-side, that is a thin sliver squeezed into whatever gap remains, not centered and not\n105\t/// where a user would naturally click. Measured on a real 4-guardrail task container: the anchor\n106\t/// covered 0.44% of the container's area, in a narrow strip near the container's right edge, and\n107\t/// none of 4 realistic click points (dead-center, near-title, left-margin, bottom-strip) landed on\n108\t/// it — dead-center instead landed on a leaf guardrail box's own click target and opened THAT\n109\t/// guardrail's source file instead of the task folder. Forcing the anchor wider via a padded label\n110\t/// does not fix this either (verified): dagre still packs it into its own slot rather than centering\n111\t/// or spanning it, and a content-dense container has almost no empty background region to reliably\n112\t/// overlay in the first place. This whole \"shape the anchor node's content to control its size/\n113\t/// position\" direction was abandoned as unfixable via the Mermaid-source anchor-node mechanism.\n114\t/// </para>\n115\t/// <para>\n116\t/// <b>The fix: an SVG overlay on the container's TITLE/LABEL ROW, injected via JavaScript AFTER\n117\t/// Mermaid's render completes.</b> Mermaid always renders a cluster (task container) as\n118\t/// <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster\" id=\"...\"&gt;</c> with exactly two children: a background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c>\n119\t/// and a <c>&lt;g class=\"cluster-label\"&gt;</c> (the title text) — the label always sits in its own\n120\t/// reserved header strip ABOVE where any leaf node begins (measured on a real container: label\n121\t/// spanned y=310.06→341.4, first leaf node did not start until y=373.7 — a genuine ~32px full-width\n122\t/// gap). This band is empty BY CONSTRUCTION regardless of how many/how large a task's checks are, so\n123\t/// it is a reliable click target no matter how content-dense the container is — unlike a dagre-packed\n124\t/// interior node. <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s embedded script (never\n125\t/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/>/this Mermaid SOURCE, which stays exactly the container-model shape\n126\t/// issue #210 left it) computes, for every task container, a full-width band from the container's\n127\t/// bounding box down to just past the label's bottom edge, and appends a real\n128\t/// <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c> covering that\n129\t/// band as the cluster group's LAST child — appended (not inserted first), so it paints ON TOP of\n130\t/// the cluster's own background rect (the cluster's only two original children) while still living\n131\t/// in a different top-level SVG group from every leaf node's own clickable <c>&lt;a&gt;</c>, so it can\n132\t/// never occlude or be occluded by a leaf-node click target. The Mermaid source contributes NO\n133\t/// anchor node, NO <c>:::invisible</c> classDef, and no <c>click</c> directive for the container at\n134\t/// all now — the task→folder path data the overlay script needs is threaded through as a small\n135\t/// embedded JSON side-table (see <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>), not a Mermaid <c>click</c>\n136\t/// directive. Leaf check-node clicks are completely unaffected — they still use Mermaid's native\n137\t/// <c>click href</c> mechanism, which already works.\n138\t/// </para>\n139\t/// <para>\n140\t/// A task-level preflight still gates its producer's <c>dependsOn</c> edge: the edge remains\n141\t/// drawn container→container exactly as any other dependency edge, and the preflight renders as an\n142\t/// ordinary check node inside the consumer's own container (before its guardrail check nodes) —\n143\t/// it is never re-routed to originate from the preflight node itself.\n144\t/// </para>\n145\t/// <para>\n146\t/// Line breaks are emitted as an explicit <c>\\n</c> (never\n147\t/// <see cref=\"StringBuilder.AppendLine()\"/>, which writes <c>Environment.NewLine</c> = CRLF\n148\t/// on Windows). This keeps <see cref=\"Render\"/>, <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>, and the\n149\t/// <c>--stdout</c> output byte-identical on every OS, so the committed <c>diagram.md</c>\n150\t/// few-shot reference never churns between a Windows and a Linux regeneration (issue #3).\n151\t/// </para>\n152\t/// </remarks>\n153\tpublic static class MermaidRenderer\n154\t{\n155\t    private const string PlanPreflightsId = \"plan_preflights\";\n156\t    private const string PlanGuardrailsId = \"plan_guardrails\";\n157\t\n158\t    /// <summary>\n159\t    /// The legend text placed OUTSIDE the Mermaid graph (see class remarks, \"Legend lives\n160\t    /// outside the Mermaid graph\"). States both the colour mapping and the before/after timing —\n161\t    /// a bare category name would not preserve the ordering semantic the removed nested boxes used\n162\t    /// to convey visually. Consumed by <c>GraphCommand</c> (a plain Markdown block placed after the\n163\t    /// fenced <c>```mermaid```</c> block in <c>diagram.md</c>) and by <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>\n164\t    /// (rendered into the HTML overlay div for <c>diagram.html</c>). Public because both consumers\n165\t    /// live outside this assembly's <c>InternalsVisibleTo</c> set (the CLI project). Deliberately NOT\n166\t    /// part of <see cref=\"Render\"/>/<see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>'s returned Mermaid source or\n167\t    /// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> — see class remarks.\n168\t    /// </summary>\n169\t    public const string LegendMarkdown =\n170\t        \"**Legend**\\n\\n\"\n171\t        + \"- 🟣 **Preflight** — verified BEFORE the task's attempt loop; gates entry \"\n172\t        + \"(dependency-delivery precondition)\\n\"\n173\t        + \"- 🟡 **Guardrail** — verified AFTER the task's action; must pass for the task to finish\\n\"\n174\t        + \"- 🟢 Plan-level containers (\\\"Full Flight Checks\\\" top, \\\"Terminal Gate\\\" bottom) run the \"\n175\t        + \"same two checks once for the whole plan, at the very start and very end.\\n\";\n176\t\n177\t    // Container fills applied per-container via a `style <id> …` statement (NOT a\n178\t    // `class <id> <className>;` statement). In Mermaid 11.4.1 a `class` assignment does NOT reach\n179\t    // a subgraph that is itself an edge endpoint — and every container is an edge endpoint under\n180\t    // the subgraph→subgraph edge model (issue #210) — whereas a `style <id>` DOES colour it. A\n181\t    // `style <id>` also colours an EMPTY plan-level bracket, which Mermaid renders as a plain node\n182\t    // rather than a cluster; that keeps the Full Flight Checks / Terminal Gate brackets on-brand\n183\t    // even when their folder is empty. Values mirror the retired `classDef task`/`classDef\n184\t    // planLevel` fills exactly, so the rendered colours are unchanged.\n185\t    private const string TaskStyle = \"fill:#cfe8ff,stroke:#1b6ec2,color:#0b2545;\";\n186\t    private const string PlanLevelStyle = \"fill:#d4edda,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#10341a;\";\n187\t\n188\t    /// <summary>Render the plan as a Mermaid <c>flowchart TD</c> string (no trailing I/O).</summary>\n189\t    public static string Render(PlanDefinition plan)\n190\t    {\n191\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n192\t\n193\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n194\t        AppendLf(sb, \"flowchart TD\");\n195\t        AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n196\t        AppendClassDefs(sb);\n197\t        return sb.ToString();\n198\t    }\n199\t\n200\t    /// <summary>\n201\t    /// Render the plan PLUS <c>click</c> directives that open each CHECK node's source under the\n202\t    /// plan folder (a preflight/guardrail node opens its own file — issue #33). Used ONLY for the\n203\t    /// local <c>diagram.html</c> viewer:\n204\t    /// <list type=\"bullet\">\n205\t    ///   <item>GitHub renders Mermaid in a sandboxed mode that disables clicks, so these would be\n206\t    ///         inert in <c>diagram.md</c> — and the targets are <c>file://</c>-local anyway.</item>\n207\t    ///   <item>They are deliberately NOT in <c>diagram.md</c> and NOT in the staleness hash\n208\t    ///         (<see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>); the targets are derived deterministically from the\n209\t    ///         same plan, as plan-relative forward-slash paths, so the output is byte-identical on\n210\t    ///         every OS (no timestamp, no absolute path).</item>\n211\t    /// </list>\n212\t    /// A TASK CONTAINER's click target is NOT a Mermaid <c>click</c> directive at all (see class\n213\t    /// remarks, \"A task container's click target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\" — issue\n214\t    /// #232/#233 superseded, issue #235): <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s embedded script injects\n215\t    /// a title-band overlay after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/>\n216\t    /// for the folder path data. This method emits no anchor node, no <c>invisible</c> classDef, and\n217\t    /// no container <c>click</c> directive — only CHECK-node clicks, identical in shape to\n218\t    /// <see cref=\"Render\"/>'s Mermaid source plus the click lines.\n219\t    /// </summary>\n220\t    public static string RenderInteractive(PlanDefinition plan)\n221\t    {\n222\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n223\t\n224\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n225\t        AppendLf(sb, \"flowchart TD\");\n226\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n227\t        AppendClassDefs(sb);\n228\t        AppendClickDirectives(plan, nodeIdBase, sb);\n229\t        return sb.ToString();\n230\t    }\n231\t\n232\t    /// <summary>\n233\t    /// The task-id → plan-relative folder path map <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> needs to inject\n234\t    /// the title-band click overlay (see class remarks, issue #235): a task container's click target\n235\t    /// is no longer a Mermaid-source mechanism, so this is how the same path data\n236\t    /// <see cref=\"AppendClickDirectives\"/> used to feed the removed anchor's <c>click href</c> now\n237\t    /// reaches the post-render JavaScript instead — as a small embedded JSON side-table keyed by the\n238\t    /// SAME container id (<c>task_&lt;base&gt;</c>) <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/> emits, so the\n239\t    /// overlay script can look a cluster's target up by its own DOM id. Plan-relative, forward-slash\n240\t    /// paths (not OS separators, not absolute) for the same byte-identical-across-OSes reason as\n241\t    /// <see cref=\"ToPlanRelative\"/>.\n242\t    /// </summary>\n243\t    public static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> TaskFolderTargets(PlanDefinition plan)\n244\t    {\n245\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n246\t\n247\t        List<TaskNode> tasks = plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToList();\n248\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AllocateNodeIdBases(tasks);\n249\t\n250\t        var targets = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n251\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n252\t        {\n253\t            string containerId = $\"task_{nodeIdBase[task.Id]}\";\n254\t            targets[containerId] = ToPlanRelative(plan.PlanDirectory, task.Directory) + \"/\";\n255\t        }\n256\t\n257\t        return targets;\n258\t    }\n259\t\n260\t    /// <summary>\n261\t    /// The cosmetic <c>classDef</c> lines (colors) for the LEAF check nodes — preflight check\n262\t    /// and guardrail check — which reference them inline via <c>:::preflight</c>/<c>:::guardrail</c>.\n263\t    /// The task-container and plan-level-container fills are applied per-container by a\n264\t    /// <c>style &lt;id&gt; …</c> statement instead (see <see cref=\"TaskStyle\"/> /\n265\t    /// <see cref=\"PlanLevelStyle\"/>), because a <c>class</c> assignment does not reach a subgraph\n266\t    /// that is an edge endpoint in the bundled Mermaid. Shared by <see cref=\"Render\"/> and\n267\t    /// <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>; deliberately EXCLUDED from the staleness key (see\n268\t    /// <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>), which is why <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/> does not call it.\n269\t    /// No longer emits an <c>invisible</c> classDef (issue #211's anchor-node mechanism was removed\n270\t    /// entirely — issue #235; see class remarks): the task-container click target is now a\n271\t    /// post-render SVG overlay <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects via JavaScript, not a\n272\t    /// Mermaid node/class at all.\n273\t    /// </summary>\n274\t    private static void AppendClassDefs(StringBuilder sb)\n275\t    {\n276\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  classDef preflight fill:#e6d7ff,stroke:#6f42c1,color:#2e1065;\");\n277\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  classDef guardrail fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#b8860b,color:#3d2c00;\");\n278\t    }\n279\t\n280\t    /// <summary>\n281\t    /// The SEMANTIC content of the diagram: ONLY the containers + nested checks + container edges\n282\t    /// (with their drawn labels), with NO <c>flowchart TD</c> header and NO cosmetic\n283\t    /// <c>classDef</c> color definitions. This is what <see cref=\"GraphSourceHash\"/> hashes, so\n284\t    /// the staleness key tracks exactly what the diagram DRAWS (container membership, nested\n285\t    /// check labels, DAG shape) — including the PLAN-LEVEL <c>preflights/</c>/<c>guardrails/</c>\n286\t    /// folder checks, not just <c>tasks{}</c>, so editing a Terminal Gate check moves the hash\n287\t    /// too. Shares the single <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> emitter with <see cref=\"Render\"/>,\n288\t    /// so the two can never drift.\n289\t    /// </summary>\n290\t    internal static string SemanticContent(PlanDefinition plan)\n291\t    {\n292\t        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plan);\n293\t\n294\t        var sb = new StringBuilder();\n295\t        AppendNodesAndEdges(plan, sb);\n296\t        return sb.ToString();\n297\t    }\n298\t\n299\t    /// <summary>\n300\t    /// Append the container model (the semantic content) for the plan: the plan-level Full Flight\n301\t    /// Checks container, one container per task in ordinal order, the plan-level Terminal Gate\n302\t    /// container, and finally every container→container edge. The single shared emitter behind\n303\t    /// <see cref=\"Render\"/>, <see cref=\"SemanticContent\"/>, and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> —\n304\t    /// all three now emit the IDENTICAL container/node shape (issue #235 removed the interactive-only\n305\t    /// anchor node), so <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> differ ONLY in\n306\t    /// whether <c>click</c> directives for CHECK nodes are appended afterward. Returns the\n307\t    /// task-id → node-id-base map so the caller can emit click directives against the SAME node ids\n308\t    /// (the emitted bytes are unchanged whether or not the caller uses the return value).\n309\t    /// </summary>\n310\t    /// <remarks>\n311\t    /// ORDER MATTERS: every container is emitted (fully, including its <c>end</c>) BEFORE any\n312\t    /// container→container edge line. A <c>subgraph A --&gt; subgraph B</c> edge references the two\n313\t    /// container ids, so both subgraph blocks must already be declared; emitting all containers\n314\t    /// first keeps every edge's endpoints resolvable and the output deterministic.\n315\t    /// </remarks>\n316\t    private static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> AppendNodesAndEdges(PlanDefinition plan, StringBuilder sb)\n317\t    {\n318\t        var graph = new DependencyGraph(plan.Tasks);\n319\t\n320\t        // Ordinal task order throughout (repo convention).\n321\t        List<TaskNode> tasks = plan.Tasks\n322\t            .OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal)\n323\t            .ToList();\n324\t\n325\t        // Allocate an injective node-id base per task ONCE, in ordinal order: a task whose\n326\t        // sanitized id collides with an earlier one gets a deterministic _2, _3, … suffix.\n327\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase = AllocateNodeIdBases(tasks);\n328\t\n329\t        // --- plan-level \"Full Flight Checks\" container (top, ALWAYS emitted) -----------\n330\t        AppendPlanLevelContainer(sb, PlanPreflightsId, \"Full Flight Checks\", plan.PlanPreflights, \"preflight\");\n331\t\n332\t        // --- one container per task ------------------------------------------------------\n333\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n334\t        {\n335\t            AppendTaskContainer(sb, task, nodeIdBase[task.Id]);\n336\t        }\n337\t\n338\t        // --- plan-level \"Terminal Gate\" container (bottom, ALWAYS emitted) --------------\n339\t        AppendPlanLevelContainer(sb, PlanGuardrailsId, \"Terminal Gate\", plan.PlanGuardrails, \"guardrail\");\n340\t\n341\t        // --- container→container edges (every container above is already fully declared) -----\n342\t        AppendContainerEdges(graph, tasks, nodeIdBase, sb);\n343\t\n344\t        return nodeIdBase;\n345\t    }\n346\t\n347\t    /// <summary>\n348\t    /// Append a plan-level bracket container (<c>plan_preflights</c> or <c>plan_guardrails</c>):\n349\t    /// its checks (sorted ordinal by name) as small boxes inside, styled with\n350\t    /// <paramref name=\"checkClass\"/>. ALWAYS emitted, even when <paramref name=\"checks\"/> is empty\n351\t    /// — the two plan-level containers are structural brackets on the whole DAG, not conditional\n352\t    /// content. The DAG edge attaches to this container's own subgraph id (no interior anchor).\n353\t    /// </summary>\n354\t    private static void AppendPlanLevelContainer(\n355\t        StringBuilder sb,\n356\t        string containerId,\n357\t        string label,\n358\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n359\t        string checkClass)\n360\t    {\n361\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(label)}]\");\n362\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}\", checks, checkClass);\n363\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n364\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {PlanLevelStyle}\");\n365\t    }\n366\t\n367\t    /// <summary>\n368\t    /// Append one task container: its preflight leaf check node(s) (if any), THEN its guardrail\n369\t    /// leaf check node(s) — both DIRECTLY inside the container, with no nested\n370\t    /// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph (see class remarks, \"Nested boxes\n371\t    /// dropped\") — then the container's <c>style</c> fill. The DAG edge attaches to this\n372\t    /// container's own subgraph id (no interior anchor).\n373\t    /// </summary>\n374\t    /// <remarks>\n375\t    /// <b>Emission-order contract (load-bearing, tested):</b> preflight check nodes are ALWAYS\n376\t    /// emitted before guardrail check nodes within a container. This is not a rendering accident —\n377\t    /// with the nested boxes gone, source order is the only surviving signal that preflights run\n378\t    /// BEFORE the task's attempt loop and guardrails run AFTER it, so callers (and the legend) may\n379\t    /// rely on it as a stable convention.\n380\t    /// </remarks>\n381\t    /// <remarks>\n382\t    /// No anchor node of any kind is emitted here (issue #211's mechanism was removed entirely —\n383\t    /// issue #235; see class remarks). <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> now\n384\t    /// emit byte-identical container/node shape for every task; the container's click target lives\n385\t    /// entirely in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s post-render JavaScript overlay instead.\n386\t    /// </remarks>\n387\t    private static void AppendTaskContainer(StringBuilder sb, TaskNode task, string @base)\n388\t    {\n389\t        string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n390\t\n391\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(task.Id)}]\");\n392\t\n393\t        // Preflights BEFORE guardrails — see remarks: this order is the emission-order contract\n394\t        // that now carries the \"before the attempt loop\" / \"after the action\" temporal semantic\n395\t        // the removed nested boxes used to convey visually.\n396\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_pf\", task.Preflights, \"preflight\");\n397\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_gr\", task.Guardrails, \"guardrail\");\n398\t\n399\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n400\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {TaskStyle}\");\n401\t    }\n402\t\n403\t    /// <summary>\n404\t    /// Append <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by name, for input-order independence) as\n405\t    /// <c>{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[label]:::{checkClass}</c> node lines, one per check. Drawn label\n406\t    /// is ALWAYS <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Name\"/> — the check's own short, stable identifier\n407\t    /// (the file-derived name, e.g. <c>01-core-tests-green-excluding-target</c>), never the\n408\t    /// (possibly long) <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/>. A prior version drew the\n409\t    /// description (truncated for task-level preflights only, issue #211) — the owner asked\n410\t    /// instead for the same short, meaningful identifier every box's click target already opens,\n411\t    /// uniformly for every check kind at both scopes (issue #222). The full description remains\n412\t    /// reachable via the node's <c>click</c> tooltip in <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> (issue\n413\t    /// #33's existing click mechanism, unaffected by this change) — no truncation heuristic is\n414\t    /// needed anywhere now.\n415\t    /// </summary>\n416\t    private static void AppendCheckNodes(\n417\t        StringBuilder sb,\n418\t        string indent,\n419\t        string nodeIdPrefix,\n420\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n421\t        string checkClass)\n422\t    {\n423\t        int ordinal = 0;\n424\t        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n425\t        {\n426\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"{indent}{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[{Quote(check.Name)}]:::{checkClass}\");\n427\t            ordinal++;\n428\t        }\n429\t    }\n430\t\n431\t    /// <summary>\n432\t    /// Append every container→container edge: the plan-preflights container into each DAG ROOT\n433\t    /// task's container (a task with no <c>dependsOn</c>), one edge per <c>dependsOn</c>\n434\t    /// relationship between two task containers, and each DAG LEAF task's container (a task nothing\n435\t    /// depends on) into the plan-guardrails container. The edge references the container's own\n436\t    /// subgraph id, so Mermaid clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER (issue #210). A\n437\t    /// task-level preflight does not change this — the gated dependency edge is drawn exactly like\n438\t    /// any other; the preflight is only ever a check node inside the consumer's own container\n439\t    /// (emitted before the container's guardrail check nodes — see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>).\n440\t    /// </summary>\n441\t    private static void AppendContainerEdges(\n442\t        DependencyGraph graph,\n443\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n444\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase,\n445\t        StringBuilder sb)\n446\t    {\n447\t        foreach (TaskNode root in tasks.Where(t => t.DependsOn.Count == 0))\n448\t        {\n449\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  {PlanPreflightsId} --> task_{nodeIdBase[root.Id]}\");\n450\t        }\n451\t\n452\t        foreach (TaskNode dependency in tasks)\n453\t        {\n454\t            foreach (string dependentId in graph.DependentsOf(dependency.Id)\n455\t                         .OrderBy(id => id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n456\t            {\n457\t                AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[dependency.Id]} --> task_{nodeIdBase[dependentId]}\");\n458\t            }\n459\t        }\n460\t\n461\t        foreach (TaskNode leaf in tasks.Where(t => graph.DependentsOf(t.Id).Count == 0))\n462\t        {\n463\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[leaf.Id]} --> {PlanGuardrailsId}\");\n464\t        }\n465\t    }\n466\t\n467\t    /// <summary>\n468\t    /// Append <c>click</c> directives (HTML-viewer only; see <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>) for\n469\t    /// every CHECK node — plan-level or task-level, preflight or guardrail — opening its own file\n470\t    /// as a plan-relative, forward-slash <c>file://</c> target resolved relative to\n471\t    /// <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root, opened in a new tab (<c>_blank</c>) so the diagram\n472\t    /// stays put. Emitted in the same ordinal/sorted order as the nodes for determinism, and using\n473\t    /// the SAME node-id scheme as <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> so every click target actually\n474\t    /// exists. A task-level preflight's click tooltip carries its FULL description (not just its\n475\t    /// name) since <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> draws only a truncated label for it — the\n476\t    /// tooltip is the click-for-detail mechanism that keeps the full text from being lost.\n477\t    /// </summary>\n478\t    /// <remarks>\n479\t    /// <b>No container click directive is emitted here (issue #235).</b> A task container's click\n480\t    /// target is no longer a Mermaid mechanism at all — see class remarks, \"A task container's click\n481\t    /// target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\". <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects it via\n482\t    /// JavaScript after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> for the\n483\t    /// folder path data. Leaf check-node clicks are unaffected here: they still target the leaf node\n484\t    /// itself, which Mermaid DOES wrap in a real clickable <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>.\n485\t    /// </remarks>\n486\t    private static void AppendClickDirectives(\n487\t        PlanDefinition plan, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase, StringBuilder sb)\n488\t    {\n489\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanPreflights, PlanPreflightsId, sb);\n490\t\n491\t        foreach (TaskNode task in plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n492\t        {\n493\t            string @base = nodeIdBase[task.Id];\n494\t            string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n495\t\n496\t            if (task.Preflights.Count > 0)\n497\t            {\n498\t                AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Preflights, $\"{containerId}_pf\", sb);\n499\t            }\n500\t\n501\t            AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Guardrails, $\"{containerId}_gr\", sb);\n502\t        }\n503\t\n504\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanGuardrails, PlanGuardrailsId, sb);\n505\t    }\n506\t\n507\t    /// <summary>\n508\t    /// Append one <c>click</c> directive per check in <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by\n509\t    /// name, mirroring <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> exactly so the ordinal-suffixed node id each\n510\t    /// click targets is the one actually emitted for that check). The tooltip is ALWAYS\n511\t    /// <c>Description ?? Name</c> in full, for every check kind at both scopes — since the drawn\n512\t    /// label is now always the short <c>Name</c> (issue #222), the tooltip is the one place the\n513\t    /// full description lives; there is no longer a \"some checks get the full text, others don't\"\n514\t    /// distinction.\n515\t    /// </summary>\n516\t    private static void AppendCheckClicks(\n517\t        PlanDefinition plan,\n518\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n519\t        string nodeIdPrefix,\n520\t        StringBuilder sb)\n521\t    {\n522\t        int ordinal = 0;\n523\t        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n524\t        {\n525\t            string checkPath = ToPlanRelative(plan.PlanDirectory, check.Path);\n526\t            string tooltipText = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(check.Description) ? check.Name : check.Description!;\n527\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  click {nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal} href \\\"{checkPath}\\\" \\\"{ClickTooltip(tooltipText)}\\\" _blank\");\n528\t            ordinal++;\n529\t        }\n530\t    }\n531\t\n532\t    /// <summary>\n533\t    /// A plan-folder-relative, forward-slash path for a <c>click href</c> target. Forward slashes\n534\t    /// (not OS separators) keep the generated <c>diagram.html</c> byte-identical across OSes and\n535\t    /// make the href resolve relative to <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root.\n536\t    /// </summary>\n537\t    private static string ToPlanRelative(string planDirectory, string absolutePath) =>\n538\t        Path.GetRelativePath(planDirectory, absolutePath)\n539\t            .Replace('\\\\', '/')\n540\t            .Replace(\"\\\"\", \"%22\", StringComparison.Ordinal); // \" is legal in Linux filenames; URL-encode to keep the click directive parseable\n541\t\n542\t    /// <summary>\n543\t    /// Make a label safe inside a double-quoted Mermaid <c>click</c> tooltip: collapse any line\n544\t    /// break to a space (a <c>click</c> directive is line-oriented, so a raw newline — now\n545\t    /// possible here since a task-level preflight's tooltip can carry its full, sometimes\n546\t    /// multi-line, description — would silently truncate or corrupt the directive) and escape\n547\t    /// embedded double quotes.\n548\t    /// </summary>\n549\t    private static string ClickTooltip(string text) =>\n550\t        text\n551\t            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n552\t            .Replace(\"\\r\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n553\t            .Replace(\"\\n\", \" \", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n554\t            .Replace(\"\\\"\", \"&quot;\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n555\t\n556\t    /// <summary>\n557\t    /// Append <paramref name=\"line\"/> followed by an explicit <c>'\\n'</c>. Used everywhere a\n558\t    /// line is emitted INSTEAD of <see cref=\"StringBuilder.AppendLine(string)\"/>, whose\n559\t    /// <c>Environment.NewLine</c> would inject CRLF on Windows and make the rendered diagram\n560\t    /// (and its source hash) platform-dependent (issue #3).\n561\t    /// </summary>\n562\t    private static void AppendLf(StringBuilder sb, string line) => sb.Append(line).Append('\\n');\n563\t\n564\t    // --- node id helpers --------------------------------------------------------------\n565\t\n566\t    /// <summary>\n567\t    /// Build the task-id → node-id-base map for <paramref name=\"tasks\"/> (already ordinal),\n568\t    /// guaranteeing distinct bases even when two task ids <see cref=\"Sanitize\"/> to the same\n569\t    /// string (e.g. <c>a.b</c> and <c>a_b</c> both → <c>a_b</c>). The first claimant keeps the\n570\t    /// readable sanitized base; later collisions get a deterministic <c>_2</c>, <c>_3</c>, …\n571\t    /// suffix in ordinal order. Every node/container family for a task (the container itself and\n572\t    /// its preflight/guardrail check nodes) derives from this unique base, so all ids stay\n573\t    /// collision-free. Also used by <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> so its JSON side-table is keyed\n574\t    /// by the SAME container id this method produces for <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/>.\n575\t    /// </summary>\n576\t    private static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> AllocateNodeIdBases(IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks)\n577\t    {\n578\t        var bases = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n579\t        var taken = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n580\t\n581\t        foreach (TaskNode task in tasks)\n582\t        {\n583\t            string candidate = Sanitize(task.Id);\n584\t            if (!taken.Add(candidate))\n585\t            {\n586\t                int suffix = 2;\n587\t                string disambiguated;\n588\t                do\n589\t                {\n590\t                    disambiguated = $\"{candidate}_{suffix}\";\n591\t                    suffix++;\n592\t                }\n593\t                while (!taken.Add(disambiguated));\n594\t\n595\t                candidate = disambiguated;\n596\t            }\n597\t\n598\t            bases[task.Id] = candidate;\n599\t        }\n600\t\n601\t        return bases;\n602\t    }\n603\t\n604\t    /// <summary>\n605\t    /// Turn an id into a safe Mermaid node-id fragment: every character that is not an ASCII\n606\t    /// letter, digit, or underscore becomes <c>_</c> (so kebab <c>-</c> → <c>_</c>).
